Additional details: Resident of Elmhurst, IL; Sister is co-defendant; Indicted via bill of information; "Sentenced 11/22/22 to 30 months of probation, $2,000 fine, $500 restitution."
Short narrative: On July 28, 2022, Kimberly DiFrancesco, 54, of Elmhurst, Illinois, and her sister, Trudy Castle, 57, of Chicago, Illinois, were both charged with Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building for their actions at the United States Capitol on January 6, 2021. They--along with Castle's adult son--traveled to Washington, D.C. together to protest the certification of the 2020 Presidential Election Results. There, they joined the mob that swarmed the U.S. Capitol, illegally entering the building through the Senate wing door. The pair walked through the building's north side and through the visitor's center, with Castle waving two small American flags and DiFrancesco communicating with others on a handheld radio. After parading about the interior of the building for about forty minutes, the sisters exited the way they entered. The pair were identified after the FBI received a tip from the spouse of an acquaintance DiFrancesco sent media from the event to; this led the FBI to identify the two of them in footage from the event.

Schwemmer, who attended the protest with her friend Jennifer Ruth Parks, 57, entered the Capitol building through broken-down doors before singing the national anthem on the second floor. Schwemmer accepted a plea deal in which she plead guilty to 40:5104(e)(2)(D) Violent Entry and Disorderly Conduct and Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building. On January 10, 2022, Schwemmer was sentenced to two years' probation, 60 hours of community service, and $500.00 restitution.

In a subsequent interview with the FBI, Sanders admitted that he had entered the Capitol and had taken pictures and videos while inside. His presence was corroborated by Capitol security footage from that day.

Blauser accepted a plea deal and plead guilty to one out of five counts. He is scheduled for sentencing on 3 February 2022.

Zlab, co-owner of a commercial concrete company, admitted to entering the Capitol and taking photos, which he later posted on Facebook, the FBI stated.

Juran has since expressed his regret for participating in the uprising."

On Parler, he wrote "We have got to get to DC on January 6th it is IMPERATIVE every single person that VOTED for Trump has to flood DC." His presence in the Capitol was corroborated by CCTV footage inside the building and Gmail account data.

Name of case: United States of America v. Brittiany Angelina Dillon
Charges: 40:5104(e)(2)(D) Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building
Additional details: Resident of MD; Indicted by Bill of Information; 60 days home detention, 3 years probation, $500 restitution
Short narrative: Brittiany Angelina Dillon, 35 of California, plead guilty to Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building and Grounds and was sentenced to three years of probation. "Dillon texted back and forth with accused rioter Bryan Betancur in the days leading up to the riot and on Jan. 6, according to federal charging documents. The pair had been texting back and forth about election fraud and plans to attend the rally in the days leading up to the siege at the Capitol. "I was there. I got pepper sprayed at the door of the capitol and tear gassed 3 times making my way up to it," she stated in one text on Jan. 6. "I fought hard .. I fell in the door and they tried to beat me with batons so I backed off and they pepper sprayed my eyes." Video footage from the Capitol shows her pushing through the crowd trying to get into the Capitol, and at one point she fell over the threshold, an FBI agent stated in the documents. She pushed forward against law enforcement again but was eventually repelled by an officer with a baton." (USA Today)

Charges: *18:1752(a)(1) - Entering and remaining in a restricted building or grounds; *18:1752(a)(2) - Disorderly and disruptive conduct in a restricted building or grounds; *40:5104(e)(2)(D) - Disorderly conduct in a Capitol building; 40:5104(e)(2)(G) - Parading, demonstrating, or picketing in a Capitol building;

William Michael Sywak revealed his son involvement in his interview with the FBI, and federal law enforcement soon identified his son in footage thereafter. The pair were seen entering and illegally walking about the interior of the U.S. Capitol.

Name of case: United States of America v. Michael Joseph Rusyn
Charges: 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building

He has been charged with Entering and remaining in a restricted building or grounds, Disorderly and disruptive conduct in a restricted building or grounds, Disorderly conduct in a Capitol building, and Parading, demonstrating, or picketing in a Capitol building. He is a volunteer firefighter and EMT. He pleaded not guilty to all counts on 4/26. Rusyn told investigators that he was actually injured himself while there when he was trying to take weapons away from members of the crowd, such as a broom stick with hooks and nails affixed to the end of it.

Name of case: United States of America v. Carey Jon Walden

A veteran of both the Navy and the Marine Corps, Walden was identified via a tip provided to the FBI as well as a Facebook post from Walden himself. In voluntary communication with law enforcement, Walden provided the photos he took during the event and also described his activities. Evidently, Walden entered the U.S. Capitol building through a broken window and illegally walked about the interior without breaking anything before leaving.

Name of case: United States of America v. Tanner Bryce Sells
Charges: 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building

He was identified after images of him walking throughout the Capitol interior on the day in question were matched with the picture from his Oklahoma drivers license. Sells walked about the Capitol and documented the goings-on inside with his cell phone, later posting some of the footage online.

Name of case: United States of America v. Wilson & Wilson

Wilson was indicted on September 14, 2021 and charged alongside his wife for their involvement in the January 2021 Capitol riot. Both plead guilty to the charge of 40:5104(e)(2)(G) - Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building. Sentencing data is pending.

Name of case: United States of America v. Brandon Straka
Charges: 40:5104(e)(2)(D) Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building
Additional details: Resident of NY; "Sentenced 1/24/22 to 36 months of probation, including three months of home detention, $5,000 fine, $500 restitution."
Short narrative: Brandon Straka, 45 of New York, plead guilty to Engaging in Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in the Capitol Building or Grounds and was sentenced to 36 months probation. Straka was charged after the FBI received a tip that he had posted videos and comments on his Twitter of his participation in the Capitol riot. He is the founder of #WalkAway Campaign, a movement to discourage liberal participation as a former liberal himself. He spoke at the rally the day before the riot and also invoked the QAnon slogan "Where we go one we go all" at the Jan 6 Stop the Steal rally in D.C.

Name of case: United States of America v. Jacob Kyle Wiedrich
Charges: 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building

Short narrative: Jacob Kyle Wiedrich, 23 of Utah, plead guilty to Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building and was sentenced to three years of probation for his role in the Capitol riot. He posted a SnapChat video where he screams, "It's wartime!... Charge! Charge the motherf***er!....We ride for Trump, we die for Trump!" under the username of “Jacob Weed.” "Wiedrich wore a red "Make America Great Again" hat and a T-shirt with a partial picture of the space shuttle. According to the FBI, footage shows Wiedrich entering the Capitol through a broken window, and once inside, he is seen screaming and taunting a police officer. He was apparently so confrontational that another member of the mob is seen restraining him. He was arrested in Salt Lake City." (NPR)

Name of case: United States of America v. Robert Ballesteros
Charges: 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building

Short narrative: Robert Ballesteros, 27 of New York, plead guilty to Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building and was sentenced to 36 months of probation for his role in the Capitol Raid. "On Jan. 6, Robert Ballesteros posted a video on his Instagram account from inside the U.S. Capitol, according to court documents. The next day, a person who had known him for years turned him into the FBI, which later recovered a conversation on his Instagram account. In the exchange, Ballesteros is asked whether he stormed the building. He replies: "Put my foot in that door" and "Made my stand."" (NPR)

Name of case: United States of America v. Ferrigno & Connor
Charges: 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building
Additional details: Resident of NY; Indicted by a Bill of Information; "Sentenced 9/15/2022 to 12 months of probation, including two months of home confinement, $371 fine, $500 restitution, 60 hours of community service."
Short narrative: Antonio Ferrigno, 26, and his co-defendant Francis Connor who both reside in Brooklyn, New York plead guilty to Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol building. He was sentenced to 12 months probation. "The FBI identified Antonio Ferrigno Jr. in an Instagram photo posted by Anton Lunyk, who is also charged in the Jan. 6, 2021, insurrection. The photo shows Ferrigno posing inside the U.S. Capitol alongside Lunyk and another man charged in the riot, Francis Connor, court documents indicate. In text messages obtained by the FBI and sent by Ferrigno to Lunyk, Ferrigno denied being inside the Capitol. In one message, he claimed an earlier video he sent of Connor climbing out a Senate Wing window, was "air dropped" to him, court documents indicate. In another, he reportedly wrote: "I wasn't in the Capitol so idc." However, the FBI identified him in security camera footage from inside the building and in the background of a video shot by the far-right figure known as "Baked Alaska," according to court documents." (NPR)

Name of case: United States of America v. Ferrigno & Connor
Charges: 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building
Additional details: Resident of NY; Indicted by a Bill of Information; "Sentenced 9/15/ 22 to 12 months of probation, including three months of home confinement, $371 fine, $500 restitution, 60 hours of community service."
Short narrative: Francis Connor, 23, and his co-defendant Antonio Ferrigno who both reside in Brooklyn, New York plead guilty to Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol building for his involvement in the Capitol riot. He was sentenced to 12 months probation. "Law enforcement identified Francis Connor in an Instagram photo posted by another person charged in the Jan. 6, 2021, riot, Anton Lunyk. The photo allegedly shows Connor, Lunyk and a third man charged, Antonio Ferrigno Jr., standing inside the U.S. Capitol. The FBI was able to link both Connor and Ferrigno to the photo based on the email addresses used to log into Instagram, court documents indicate. Connor and Ferrigno also reportedly appear in a Live Streamed video shot by the far-right media personality known as "Baked Alaska." In a group message on Instagram with Lunyk and Ferrigno, Connor also allegedly wrote, "I was in the Capitol building."" (NPR)

A federal magistrate judge authorized a search warrant for the email of Schubert’s wife that reportedly placed them both inside the building. Schubert was released on bond." (NPR)

Schubert from Crest Hill, IL, plead guilty to Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building for her role in the Capitol raid. She was sentenced to 18 months probation. "Schubert is seen on footage taken within the building, wearing a black jacket with the text "Plumbers & Pipefitters Local Union 422 Joliet IL" on the back, court documents say. A federal magistrate judge authorized a search warrant for her email account that reportedly showed she was present inside the Capitol on that day. A neighbor told a local CBS station that the Crest Hill, Ill., couple had posted Trump signs on public property multiple times." (NPR)

Both women have plead guilty to the single charge of parading, demonstrating or picketing in a Capitol building. As they await sentencing, they have been ordered to $500.00 in restitution for damage to the Capitol building.

Name of case: United States of America v. Christopher Michael Cunningham
Charges: 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building

The FBI received tips that Cunningham had breached the Capitol building, which was corroborated by CCTV footage inside the Capitol. Cunningham was further identified by cell phone records and photos of him inside the building.

Name of case: United States of America v. Justin McAuliffe
Charges: 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building

Short narrative: Justin McAuliffe, 39 of New York, plead guilty to knowingly entering or remaining in any restricted building or grounds without lawful authority and was sentenced to 3 years of probation for his role entering the Capitol Raid. McAuliffe was the subject of numerous tips submitted the FBI call centers based on his Facebook posts. FBI agents were able to locate McAuliffe's Telegram and Facebook, both of which contains his picture and real name. The Facebook posts shows McAuliffe in front of the US Capitol and a crowd waving Trump flags, and his other posts reads "yeah I was in one of the offices...Cops came in and weee [sic] like Okay guys really? They didn't even ask us to leave right away. They let us sit down and hang out and relax." A picture of him was taken in a member of Congress' office, which he later used as his Telegram profile picture. His location inside the Capitol was further corroborated by his phone records. (Statement of Facts)

Name of case: United States of America v. Steven Thurlow
Charges: 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building
Additional details: Indicted by a Bill of Information; Resident of MI.; "Sentenced 8/30/22 to 24 months of probation, 80 hours of community service, and $500 in restitution."
Short narrative: Steven Thurlow, 50 of Michigan, plead guilty to Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building for his role in the Capitol Raid."A witness contacted the FBI identifying Steven Thurlow as having been inside the Capitol building on Jan. 6, according to court documents. "The witness also provided screenshots of Thurlow’s Facebook posts, including one in which he is seen wearing camouflage tactical gear with a “Boogaloo” patch on his chest. The extremist Boogaloo movement anticipates a second civil war in America, and some adherents even seek to bring about that conflict. “Ahh nothing like a new pair of 511’s and fresh set of level IV SAPI’s in the plate carrier to go “peacefully protest” with, the caption to the picture read, referring to a high-level ballistic body armor plate, Thurlow had allegedly purchased. According to the FBI, Thurlow served in the Army from 1988 until 1991. A second witness told the FBI that Thurlow had become something of a “conspiracy theorist” after joining the military. Inside the Capitol building, photos show Thurlow lying on what appears to be a conference room table. He is also seen walking around the hallways recording on his cell phone, wearing a camouflage jacket, a yellow scarf and white rimmed sunglasses.""(NPR) He served in the US Army 101st Airborne 1988-1991, served abroad in Saudi Arabia for 6 months in 1990.

Name of case: United States of America v. Julia Jeanette Sizer
Charges: 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building

Short narrative: Julia Sizer, 38, a resident of Pennsylvania, plead guilty to Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building for her role in the Capitol Raid. Her husband, Brian Douglas Sizer was also arrested. According to NPR, "Julia Sizer came to the attention of the FBI via a tip from a person who'd obtained a video allegedly taken by the defendant that showed her "in the [U.S.] capitol building during the insurrection," court documents indicate. The criminal complaint says that after reviewing the video, agents reached out to Sizer, who denied being in the Capitol at the time of the Jan. 6, 2021, riot and subsequently acquired counsel. Sizer's phone was not shown to be among those that showed up in records provided by Google in a search warrant, but after a later interview with the FBI in the presence of her legal counsel, she admitted she was inside the Capitol on Jan. 6, 2021."

Name of case: United States of America v. Jason Michael Comeau
Charges: 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building
Additional details: Resident of FL; Indicted by a Bill of Information; "Sentenced 11/15/22 to 12 months of probation, including 2 months of home confinement, 60 hours community service, $371 fine, $500 restitution"
Short narrative: Jason Michael Comeau, 40, a resident of Florida, plead guilty to Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building for his role in the Capitol Raid. "Less than a week after the Jan. 6 U.S. Capitol riot, a relative of Jason Comeau contacted the FBI and said that Comeau had admitted to breaching the building, according to charging documents filed in federal court. Comeau later gave a voluntary interview to FBI agents, court papers state, during which he said he had attended the pro-Trump rally earlier in the day and then marched toward the Capitol building. Comeau allegedly told agents that he climbed the stairs heading into the building and that after the crowd repeatedly chanted "Let us in," Capitol police moved aside, allowing the crowd to enter the building. Comeau allegedly told FBI agents that he believed he was allowed to enter the building and that he only progressed as far as a hallway. Prosecutors now allege that surveillance footage and cell phone video show Comeau going as far as the Capitol's Statuary Hall and remaining in the building for approximately 20 minutes. He also allegedly joined chants of "stop the steal," a slogan adopted by President Donald Trump and some of his supporters that falsely asserts that Trump won the 2020 presidential election. From July 2000 to December 2002, Comeau served in the U.S. Army as a combat engineer, an Army spokesperson confirmed to NPR. Comeau did not have any combat deployments and held the rank of private at the end of his service, the spokerson said." (NPR)

Name of case: United States of America v. Tenney & Youngers
Charges: 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building

Veteran status: Former active duty and reserve components
Short narrative: Darrell Alan Youngers of Texas traveled to Washington DC and unlawfully entered the US Capitol building with South Carolinian George Amos Tenney the III. Youngers walked around the building and laid hands on a police during an altercation. For his participation in the U.S. Capitol riot on January 6, 2021, he was charged with disorderly and disruptive conduct in a restricted building, knowingly entering or remaining in a restricted building without lawful authority, disorderly conduct in a U.S. Capitol building, and parading, demonstrating or picketing in a Capitol building.

Name of case: United States of America v. Paul Colbath
Charges: 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building
Additional details: Resident of SC; Indicted by a Bill of Information; Sentenced 4/6/22 to three years of probation, to include 30 days home detention, 60 hours community service, $500 restitution
Short narrative: In the days after the riot at the U.S. Capitol on January 6, 2021, informants reached out to the FBI informing them that Paul Gray Colbath, 64, of South Carolina had been bragging about his participation in the events there. The FBI then conducted an interview with Colbath himself, in which he confirmed that he was indeed present in Washington D.C. on the day in question and did indeed enter the U.S. Capitol Building with the violent crowd. While inside, he witnessed vandalism and the usage of tear gas; he ushered another protestor, clearly affected by the tear gas, out of the commotion and into a nearby office. Colbath claims he left the building soon after. Footage provided by Colbath himself as well as closed circuit surveillance footage from within the building confirm all that he told the FBI; additionally, records from T-Mobil tracked the cell phone using the number associated with Colbath to the interior of the U.S. Capitol on the day in question. With all this information, Colbath was charged by the U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia.

Name of case: United States of America v. Traci J. Sunstrum
Charges: 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building

Short narrative: Traci J. Name of case: United States of America v. Pettit & Burress
Charges: 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building
Additional details: Resident of OH; Partner also arrested; Indicted by a Bill of Information, sentenced to 18 months of probation, including 45 days of home detention, 60 hours of community service and $500 restitution
Short narrative: On December 27, 2021, Gabriel Burress, 22, and his partner Madison Pettit, 19, of Swanton, Ohio, were both indicted as co-defendants in a bill of information for their activities at the U.S. Capitol on January 6, 2021. Footage from CCTV and other recording devices within the U.S. Capitol Building showed the pair entering the Rotunda with the rest of the crowd and walking about the interior for about ten minutes before leaving. On their way out, Burress joined in a chant with the rest of the protestors, and Pettit later sent a text message disparaging the police officers on the scene by calling them "stupid ass Capitol police part of the swamp bad cops." The FBI became aware of the couple thanks to an online tip. Investigation linked their cell phone numbers to the U.S. Capitol's cellular service site on January 6th; their appearances in their social media and drivers license images also matched those that were captured in the footage from the event. This investigation culminated in an interview with the two where they confirmed their presence at the Capitol riot on the day in question.

After being inside the Rotunda for approximately five minutes, Vincent left through the same door she entered through. Additional details: Indicted by a Bill of Information; Sentenced 5/10/22 to 36 months’ probation, including 30 days’ home detention, 100 hours of community service, $500 restitution.
Short narrative: On February 16, 2022, Nicholas Lentz, 42, a combat veteran of the U.S. Marine Corps and former police officer from North Miami Beach, Florida was charged for his role during the Capitol protests by a bill of information. Lentz was quickly identified by the FBI after two tipsters sent in photos and videos of him participating in the riot; one of these supplementary pieces of evidence was a fifty-two-second video clip posted to Lentz's Facebook account speaking in the Crypt, saying in-part "America has spoken. You can not stop millions of people. Cannot stop it." Lentz was later identified in the Miami Herald by former North Miami Beach Mayor Anthony DeFillipo. Lentz was interviewed by the FBI, in which he admitted to entering the United States Capitol but asserting that he did not partake in any violence. Additionally, surveillance footage from within the United States Capitol interior confirms that Lentz paraded throughout the building for almost an hour. He was initially arrested on February 19, 2021 in the Southern District of Florida and was later placed on personal recognizance bond.

Riley has worked for the Capitol Police for nearly 25 years and most recently served as a technician with the K-9 unit. There is no evidence in the indictment that Riley has links to any known extremist organizations. Riley was not himself present at the U.S. Capitol during the events that occurred there on January 6, 2021; he was responding to pipe bomb threats around the Democratic and Republican headquarters. However, after January 6, Riley contacted someone on Facebook who had made posts claiming that he was inside the U.S. Capitol Building on the day in question. Riley encouraged the Facebook friend to hide any indications that he had been in the building, because that would cause them to investigate and charge him. Later, Riley learned that this individual made the FBI aware of their communications, so he deleted the messages and sent new ones as a cover-up.

Short narrative: Felipe Marquez, 25, was arrested and charged with knowingly entering the Capitol Building or the grounds of it without lawful authority as well as violent entry and disorderly conduct with regards to the January 6, 2021 Capitol protests. According to the South Florida Sun Sentinel, Marquez made his way up to Washington, D.C., for planned rallies in support of former President Donald Trump on Jan. 6. Throughout the trip, Marquez, 25, shot a series of clips on Snapchat while driving his Tesla and vaping. A longtime ride-share driver, Marquez said he went to D.C. to protest the “normalization of prostitution” and Communism. He said he became a Trump supporter after learning more about economic disparities between races and policies that he believed helped close them. He felt dismayed by the way Trump was treated in office. “I feel Trump was done like Richard Nixon but to a greater scale.” In D.C., Marquez uploaded clips of himself participating in outdoor rallies. Before entering the Capitol Building, Marquez uploaded a clip showing people scaling a wall on the building, according to his criminal complaint. In his very next video, he is inside a private office belonging to Sen. Jeff Merkley, of Oregon. He smokes his vape pen and shows off his red “Keep America Great” hat. On 9/10/21, Marquez plead guilty to Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds and was sentenced to 18 months probation, including three months of home detention, and $500 restitution.

Wilkinson was identified via a confidential human source as well as numerous images and videos taken from inside the Capitol. After being identified, Wilkinson agreed to a phone interview with agents where he acknowledged his participation in the riot. Additionally, a remorseful note was found in Wilkinson's phone stating he "regretted it since the moment I stepped foot inside" (SoF). According to court documents, he flew from his then-home in Streamwood, Illinois to Washington, D.C. to attend the "Stop the Steal" rally at the Ellipse. Afterward, he went to the U.S. Capitol Building, walked up the stairs at the Lower West Plaza, and illegally entered the building through the Upper West Terrace. He proceeded to the Rotunda, where he took pictures. He then went up to the third floor and entered the Senate Gallery through a breech door, taking more pictures all the while. Afterward, he returned to the Rotunda and then left through East Rotunda door after law enforcement officers began ushering people out.

Short narrative: On July 15, 2021, Lois Lynn McNicoll, 69 of California, was charged with numerous federal offenses for her actions at the United States Capitol on January 6, 2021. Media from the day show the individual identified as McNicoll entering the building through the Senate Wing Door, taking videos or photos with her cell phone, and walking through the Crypt before being ushered out through the Memorial Doors. Altogether, she spent just over half an hour in the U.S. Capitol Building. She was identified by two witnesses--one of whom was her coworker at the Los Angeles County Department of Public Social Services--who recognized her in media from the day in question. She was captured in video footage wearing a white "Trump" hat with the California flag draped over her shoulders; this version of the California flag read "Trump Country" instead of "California Republic."

He plead guilty to one count of Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in any of the Capitol Buildings.

Name of case: United States of America v. Logan Grover

Short narrative: On May 13, 2022, in a superseding indictment, Logan Grover, 43, of Erie, Colorado, was charged with numerous federal offenses for his role in the Capitol protests. An Army veteran, Grover made posts to Facebook on January 5, announcing his intent to stop an "insurrection" at the Capitol and that he believed violence was highly likely. This was the post that multiple tipsters used to inform the FBI of Logan Grover's involvement. Although Grover declined an FBI interview when approached in person, the agents used the description they gained in that interaction to locate him in other videos from the riot. In various videos, the individual identified as Grover is shown in various areas both inside and outside the U.S. Capitol Building. Court documents indicate that, after attending President Trump's rally at the Ellipse and eventually making it to the Capitol grounds, he illegally entered the building through the eastern Rotunda doors. He made his way past law enforcement officers with a group that pushed past them and went into the Rotunda. After being shepherded together by officers, Grover and his group left the Rotunda and then the building. Grover was inside for approximately fifteen minutes. Grover plead guilty to one charge of Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building.

Short narrative: On January 19, 2021, a tipster notified the FBI that Adam Mark Weibling, 34, of Katy, Texas was one of the rioters that breached police lines and illegally entered the U.S. Capitol on January 6, 2021. The tipster provided law enforcement with images from Weibling's social media accounts proving his presence in Washington on the day in question as well as a YouTube video of the events that show an individual matching Weibling's description participating. A second tipster also reached out to federal law enforcement about Weibling, providing his address and notifying them that he had travelled to Washington with his wife Brittany for the event; the second tipster directed the FBI to the same video that the first tipster did. In the video, the individual matching Weibling's description is shown talking to the officer attempting to hold him back from proceeding further into the U.S. Capitol building. Surveillance footage from within the building shows that Weibling then forced his way past the officer to linger about the Rotunda and Old Senate Chamber hallway. Review of flight records from America Airlines showed that Weibling did take a flight to Houston from Washington D.C. on January 7, and review of Weibling's social media activity found that the account linked to his phone number and address--where an affiant later observed Weibling physically--had engaged with posts by Mike Cernovich indicating that he and his wife would be in Washington D.C. on the day of the electoral ballot counts. Weibling was soon after arrested and charged with disorderly conduct in a restricted building.

Then, on January 6, Spain was found to have illegally entered the U.S. Capitol building with the mob in Washington D.C. He took photos of himself at the event and posted them to social media; the posts were then found by the FBI, who connected the posts to a phone number belonging to Spain and to usage of a cell site servicing the interior of the U.S. Capitol Building on the day in question. Spain was later interviewed at his Oklahoma home, where he confirmed his presence at the riot and his entrance into the United States Capitol. Spain was then charged with Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds; Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds; Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building; Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building following his participation in the Capitol riot.

Short narrative: On November 29, 2021, Michael Aaron Carico, 33, was charged with numerous federal offenses for his participation in the riot at the United States Capitol building on January 6, 2021. A confidential human source who had also been present on the U.S. Capitol grounds on the day in question provided a photo and video to the FBI that showed Carico identifying himself by name to other rioters as he moved about the Capitol grounds with a camera and a stabilizer. The video features Carico relaying his Facebook and Instagram username to others, and content on these two accounts show the same individual identified as Carico in the confidential human source video. Further, U.S. Capitol surveillance cameras captured Carico moving throughout the interior of the U.S. Capitol building. Additionally, the mobile device registered to Carico's Google account was found to have been inside the U.S. Capitol at the time in question. After a search warrant was obtained for Carico's Google account, more photos of him at sites outside the U.S. Capitol and around sites in D.C. were uncovered.

In addition to the footage, multiple records obtained by law enforcement show that Kastner traveled to an apartment in North Beach, Md., in the first week of January 2021 from his home in Ohio and then back to Ohio, where he arrived at an address belonging to Faulkner, on Jan. 7, 2021." According to video obtained by federal investigators, Homol said, "They can't stop us all, come on we are going into the Capitol, can't stop us all." In another clip, Homol allegedly declared, "We're tired of it, the communist cops of Washington, D.C, we're storming the Capitol building. ... This is our country." After the rally, he allegedly marched to the U.S. Capitol and, with co-defendant Patrick King, then smoked marijuana inside the building, according to their middle school classmate who claimed to have seen photos on Facebook and tipped off the FBI in February of 2021. Court documents also allege that Facebook records show Jones told Facebook friends he deleted anything “political” from his account and was creating a second account for only close friends and family, as he grew anxious about getting arrested for allegedly entering the Capitol. He was arrested March 23, 2022, in Seattle. (NPR)

After the airport security guard contacted the proper authorities, Lolos was arrested. He was charged with multiple counts by the U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia and eventually plead guilty to the fourth, being sentenced to 14 days of incarceration and $500 restitution.

A picture of the family trailer from Tom Munn's Facebook page appeared to show him hauling a trailer with a QAnon sign posted on the back. "On Dec. 28, 2020, Thomas Munn reportedly posted an image on Facebook that indicated that then-President Donald Trump had "requested your attendance" in Washington, D.C., on Jan. 6. According to court documents, Thomas Munn captioned the image: “Our President has only asked two things from us, so far... #1 Vote #2 January 6, 2021.” On Jan. 5, 2021, he allegedly wrote on Facebook, “We made it to our hotel just outside DC … 1,600 miles in 24 hrs!” and included a photo of a trailer passed on the highway with a sign that said, "D.C. Bound. We are Q." On the afternoon of Jan. 6, 2021, he posted a photo of himself with the four other family members charged and the child who has not been identified, court documents indicate. He reportedly wrote: "Made it back to the hotel about an hour ago . . . Have lots of pics and video to follow. ... The only damage to the capitol building was several windows and sets of doors. Nothing inside the capitol was damaged. I can tell you, patriots NEVER made it to the chamber. There was no violence in the capitol building, the crowd was NOT out of control . . . they were ANGRY!!!” Security footage from inside the Capitol that day indicate that Thomas Munn entered the building with his family, according to court documents." (NPR)

Charges: 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building
Additional details: Resident of NY; Indicted by a Bill of Information; Sentenced 4/21/22 to 36 months of probation, including 14 days in jail, 60 days of home confinement, $2,500 fine, $500 restitution.
Short narrative:
Richard Bryan Watrous, 59, a resident of New York, plead guilty to Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building for his role in the Capitol Raid. 
"Richard Watrous was initially identified from surveillance footage of the riot at the U.S. Capitol, according to a criminal complaint. FBI agents say he was wearing a distinctive red "Trump" hat when he entered the Capitol and then could be seen leaving after a few minutes inside. When he was interviewed by law enforcement, Watrous allegedly said his trip to Washington, D.C., was planned as soon as he heard former President Trump urging people to go. He allegedly said he drove to D.C. from his New York home despite the fact that he did not feel he could have any effect on the proceedings in Congress. According to court documents, Watrous attended the rally at the Ellipse the morning of Jan. 6 and then made his way to the Capitol, where he said there were already people there, and he could hear flashbangs and was aware of tear gas even though he was fairly far away from the building. When he allegedly entered the Capitol building, he told agents, he heard someone yell, "they just killed a girl!"; agents believe that the person was referring to the shooting of Ashli Babbitt. Once inside, Watrous reportedly said that he felt uncomfortable and thought, “This is crazy. What the hell is going on here?” He went on to say that people around him "seemed like troublemakers and did not seem like peaceful protestors," court documents indicate. He claims he witnessed a man who had said he was going into House Speaker Nancy Pelosi's office holding a bottle of wine and saying "I got Nancy Pelosi's wine!" Watrous told agents that he was inside the Capitol for about five minutes before he left, going back into the Rotunda briefly before returning to his hotel."' (NPR)

Short narrative: On June 23, 2023, Kimberly Dragoo, 51, and Steven Dragoo, 62, both of St. Joseph, MO, were both charged with numerous federal crimes for their role in the January 6 Capitol riot. On January 6, 2021, the Dragoos, a married couple, attended a "Stop the Steal" rally, which the Dragoos became aware of through their Facebook group, before marching with other protestors to the Northwest side of the U.S. Capitol, later breaking off from the group to take pictures on a terrace outside the Senate Wing door. They illegally walked through an inside corridor until they were blocked off by law enforcement that prevented them from going further and ordered them to go back. After leaving, the FBI became aware of the Dragoos' involvement through tipsters and the Facebook posts that Kimberly made documenting the event.

Name of case: United States of America v. Kurt Peterson
Additional details: Resident of KY; "Kurt Peterson Sentenced 11/2/23 to Forty-Five (45) Days of Incarceration followed by a term of Sixty (60) Days of Supervised Release to be served as Home Incarceration (with conditions). Short narrative: "On Jan. 10, Kurt Peterson allegedly posted a lengthy message on Facebook indicating that he had been inside the U.S. Capitol on Jan. 6. The message, detailed in court documents, begins: "To my family and friends who are able to see this, I am writing it with a voice recognition program while driving. I feel the need to keep moving and trying to keep my phone wrapped such that it can't be traced most of the time." He then described the pro-Trump rally as peaceful and loving, but added "When there are huge crowds and there are people that are inciting violence, the crowds will many times be pulled in to this action." In the post, Peterson reportedly stated that he was with three military veterans and that he was not there to hurt anybody or damage anything, but was there as a "show of solidarity to right the wrongs of the past election." According to court documents, Peterson indicated that he was there when a woman, presumably Ashli Babbitt, was fatally shot by police. Peterson reportedly added that "Non Lethal force could have been used without the lethal shot that was made by this bodyguard in the speaker's lobby" and that he offered to provide first aid but was denied. Phone records obtained from Samsung reportedly place Peterson in the Capitol that day as well. He also appeared in police body camera footage and in at least two publicly posted videos, including one from the location where Babbitt was shot, according to court documents. In one video, Peterson can allegedly be seen using his fist to smash a window on the outside of the Capitol and shouting, “This is our house. Let us in. Our house.” (NPR)

Name of case: United States of America v. Savannah Danielle McDonald, Nolan Harold Kidd

Short narrative: "Nolan Kidd and Savannah McDonald allegedly traveled together to Washington, D.C., the day before the assault on the U.S. Capitol. According to court documents, they can be seen in many of the most familiar photos of Jan. 6 -- near the man who became known as the “QAnon Shaman.” On Jan. 11, the FBI received a tip that Kidd had been inside of the Capitol building, which included a screenshot of an account believed to be his, showing an album of pictures of the day captioned, “Just made it home, I have tons of photos and videos to share with you guys.” Federal prosecutors say that agents interviewed Kidd at his home days later, and he said that “the doors to the U.S. Capitol were wide open.” A photo returned from a search of Kidd’s phone shows pictures of him and McDonald smiling for the camera, and Kidd showing a “thumbs up.” Kidd can also reportedly be seen in a video posted by the Young Patriot Society and credited to himself, alongside McDonald saying, “[W]e got in from the back.” Agents also reviewed video footage of Kidd and McDonald allegedly heading to the Upper West Terrace of the Capitol with a group of rioters that pushed through a line of law enforcement and headed into the building through a fire door. A search warrant for a Snapchat account McDonald claimed was hers returned images of a group chat in which a user believed to be Kidd reportedly says, “Me and Savannah are F***ING STORMTROOPERS.”" (NPR)

Jancart told prosecutors he entered the U.S. Capitol with Rau, and the FBI says Jancart identified Rau in photos from the Capitol. On the same day of Jancart's arrest, Rau called the U.S. Marshals Service in Columbus, Ohio, asking to turn himself in, according to court documents. Afterward, he remained in the Capitol and roamed around before leaving. "Daniel Harrington sentenced to Forty-Five (45) days of Incarceration on Count 1, no term of Supervised Release to follow. Defendant sentenced to Six (6) months of Probation on Count Six (6). Counts 1 and 6 to run consecutive. A Special Assessment fee of $35 ($25 on Count 1 and $10 on Count 6) and Restitution in the amount of $500 as to both counts. Name of case: United States of America v. Daniel Bibonge Amsini

Short narrative: Daniel Bibonge Amsini entered the U.S. Capitol building in Washington, D.C. on January 6, 2021 based on open source and social media images. He was charged with six different offenses: (1) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds; (2) Disorderly or Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds; (3) Violent Entry and Disorderly Conduct on Capitol Grounds; (4) Disorderly or Disruptive Conduct in a Capitol Building; (5) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building; (6) Theft of Government Property. Amsini was seen entering multiple parts of the building while wearing a “Make America Great Again” hat. Based on screenshots from CCTV footage, he stole an ILC Dover Scape CBRN30 escape hood from the Senate Chambers and placed it in his string bag. This object is an advanced air-purifying escape respirator that provides protection from carbon monoxide, and chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear contaminants. Based on the Statement of Facts I would identify blockading/unlawful assembly as the tactic used to target this Federal building. His motive behind taking the air purifier from the Capitol and entering the building in the first place is not explicitly said. Daniel Amsini was sentenced to Forty-Five (45) Days of Incarceration followed by Twelve (12) Months of Supervised Release (with conditions). The defendant was further Ordered to pay $749.00 Restitution and $25.00 Special Assessment. No fine was imposed.

Charges: 18:231(a)(3) Civil Disorder; 18:1752(a)(1) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 18:1752(a)(2) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 40:5104(e)(2)(D) Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building; 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building

No information on his charges is available, but court documents show he was released on a $100,000 bond with the stipulation that he submit to random drug testing and refrain from excessive use of alcohol." (USA Today). Rahm pleaded not guilty and sentencing information is pending. Rham's father, James Douglas Rham, Jr., was also arrested following his involvement at the Capitol on January 6th, 2021.

Name of case: United States of America v. Ballenger & Price
Charges: 18:1752(a)(1) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds with a Deadly or Dangerous Weapon Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 18:1752(a)(2) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 40:5104(e)(2)(D) Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building; 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building
Additional details: Resident of MD; Indicted by a Bill of Information; "Cynthia Ballenger and Christopher Price Found guilty 3/21/23 on counts 1s-4s."; "Cynthia Ballenger Sentenced 9/29/23 to four (4) months incarceration to run concurrent with all other counts, followed by nine (9) months Supervised Release as to counts 1-2 to run concurrent, Special Assessments totaling $70, and Restitution in the amount of $500."; "Christopher Price Sentenced 9/29/23 to forty-five (45) days incarceration to run concurrent with all other counts, followed by nine (9) months Supervised Release as to counts 1-2 to run concurrent, Special Assessments totaling $70, and Restitution in the amount of $500."
Short narrative: On March 8, 2022, married couple Cynthia Catherine Ballenger and Christopher John Price of Emmitsburg, Maryland, were charged in a superseding information. The FBI first identified the pair after they received an anonymous tip indicating that the two had posted photos from the event on their Facebook accounts. Although photos had been removed, comments from posts on those accounts reflected the owners confirming their commenters' questions about whether or not they were at the U.S. Capitol rioting on January 6, 2021. The phone numbers and Google accounts attached to these accounts were found to be connected to mobile devices that were detected within the U.S. Capitol Building on the day in question. Further, CCTV footage from within the building featured images of two individuals whose physical descriptions matched those of the drivers license photos found for Ballenger and Price walking about the interior of the Capitol Building. Additionally, credit card account records from January 6, provided by PNC Bank, are consistent with purchases made at locations between their home in Maryland and their destination of Washington, D.C. The FBI interviewed a friend of the two, who identified them in the photos and provided the FBI with text messages and photos sent between him and Price; the photos show them at multiple Washington D.C. sites and the texts all but confirm their participation in the violent protest. Finally, the FBI interviewed Price and Bellenger themselves, who admitted to being in the city on the day in question, but denied that they were part of the crowd that caused damage or that they were there at that time.

Name of case: United States of America v. Tony Lee Gill
Charges: 18:1752(a)(1) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds; *18:1752(a)(2) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds; *40:5104(e)(2)(D) Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building; *40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building

Short narrative: On December 21, 2023, Tony Lee Gill, 53, of Front Royal, VA, was federally charged following his participation in the January 6, 2021 Capitol riot. Gill was identified via photos and videos of Gill and Capitol CCTV footage. According to court documents, Gill drove directly to the Capitol from a work obligation, foregoing attendance at the "Stop the Steal" rally at the Ellipse. After parking his vehicle and walking the rest of the way there, Gill joined the mob on the Lower West Terrace. As he chanted along with the rest of the crowd, he took videos and photos of the event with his phone. He illegally entered the building by climbing through the broken window adjacent to the Tunnel. Gill remained in this room with other rioters until law enforcement began using flashbangs and tear gas to disperse the mob around the tunnel. At this point, Gill exited through the window and retreated to the Capitol's West Plaza, where he merged back in with the rest of the crowd. Gill was ultimately sentenced to 45 days in prison.

He illegally entered the building through the Senate Wing Doors, and walked through a senator's office, the Crypt, and other areas of the first floor before exiting the way he came in. Throughout the fifteen minutes he was inside, Fiol documented his involvement through messages and videos he took and then sent to others through Facebook Messenger. It was one of these recipients of Fiol's braggadocious messages that reported him to the FBI.

Name of case: Untied States of America v. Daniel Michael Morrissey

According to the Statement of Offense, Morrissey illegally entered the U.S. Capitol through the Rotunda door on the afternoon in question and proceeded to walk about areas of the interior, including Statutory Hall and Will Rogers Hallway. He protested outside the House Main Door before leaving the building through the Upper House Doors, having spent approximately 28 minutes inside the U.S. Capitol. Morrissey came to the attention of the FBI after a former co-worker of his reported that they had been shown photos and videos of him in the U.S. Capitol by another co-worker. Evidently, Morrisey sent these photos to the latter coworker via text message, including a selfie that was sent in response to the direct question of whether or not he was inside the U.S. Capitol on that day.

Name of case: United States of America v. Hentschel & Pryer
Charges: 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building
Verdict: Guilty on some charges/not guilty on others
Additional details: Resident of MO; Indicted by a Bill of Information; "Sentenced 9/30/22 to 45 days of incarceration, 36 months of probation, and $500 restitution."
Short narrative: Mahailya Pryer, 34, of Springfield, Missouri, travelled to Washington D.C. for the events of January 6th with Cara Maureen Hentschel and two other individuals. While the two identified individuals did not participate in the illegal riot at the U.S. Capitol Building, Pryer and Hentschel did. Photos of the two of them standing before the mob at the Capitol's threshold were posted to Hentschel's Facebook account afterwards and surveillance footage within the building caught the two people matching those in the photos walking about the Capitol interior. Hentschel was identified to the FBI by an anonymous tipster, which then led them to Pryer. Interviews with the two individuals who traveled with Hentschel and Pryer were conducted; the interviewees further identified Hentschel and Pryer in the photographs. Pryer herself declined to be asked questions. The two individuals encouraged their acquaintances to cooperate with law enforcement. Further interrogation of Hentschel's Facebook account revealed direct message conversations in which Pryer confirmed with conversants that they were inside the U.S. Capitol without proper authority. The two were arrested and charged based on this information.

The cloth appears to have the following text handwritten on it: IN MEMORY OF OUR GOD, OUR RELIGION, AND FREEDOM, AND OUR PEACE, OUR WIVES, AND OUR CHILDREN. ALMA 46:12. This is a message taken from the Book of Mormon, attributed to Captain Moroni.

Additional details: Resident of Selkirk, New York; Indicted by Bill of Information; "Sentenced 1/14/22 to 50 days of incarceration, followed by 12 months of supervised release, $1,000 fine, $500 restitution."
Short narrative: On June 21, 2021, William Tryon was indicted on charges of Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds; Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds; Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building; Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building. The defendant's made incriminating remarks on a Facebook page for a group called "Liberty Bell Alliance 76," of which Tryon is the founder, according to footage included in the complaint. Tryon accepted a plea deal in which he plead guilty to Count 1 of the charges, and was ultimately sentenced to 50 days in prison and 12 months of unsupervised released. He was also ordered to pay a $1,000.00 fine and $500.00 restitution. "A 70-year-old Coeymans man who staunchly opposes what he called "ungodly socialist forces" was arrested by the FBI on Tuesday and charged in U.S. District Court with taking part in the Jan. 6 insurrection at the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C. William Tryon, whose attendance at the Jan. 6 storming of the Capitol was caught on YouTube.com - and also by a relative who turned him in - was charged with three federal misdemeanors: knowingly entering a restricted building without authority, knowingly engaging in disorderly conduct in a restricted building and violent entry and disorderly conduct on Capitol grounds." - Times Union.

Vy is charged with Brian Healion and Isaiah Giddings, who were all allegedly part of a Telegram message with Rehl and one other unidentified person who was not in Washington, D.C., on Jan. 6, 2021. Name of case: United States of America v. Boyd Allen Camper
Charges: 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building
Additional details: Resident of MT; Indicted by BIll of Information; Sentenced to 60 days incarceration and $10 special assessment
Short narrative:
Boyd Allen Camper, 54 of Montana, plead guilty to Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building for his participation in the Capitol riot. He was sentenced to 2 months of prison. 

"Multiple witnesses confirmed to the FBI that Camper went inside the U.S. Capitol building carrying a GoPro camera on a stick. Days later, Camper told FBI agents in an interview that “in my mind, we were going to take the Capitol steps.” He also said he entered the building through a small door that led to the Rotunda and then proceeded to a room “with statues.” According to court documents, Camper told the FBI they couldn't review the footage he took on his camera if they would use the content against him. In a sentencing memorandum filed in federal court, Camper is identified as having military service. In that memo, a U.S. prosecutor wrote: "While Camper’s military service is laudable, it renders his conduct on January 6 all the more egregious. As a former military member, Camper was well aware that taxpayer status does not bestow upon a person the right to enter restricted government buildings. His voluntary decision to storm a guarded government building is nothing short of shocking in light of his former military service and training."" (NPR)

Ryan took a plea deal, pleading guilty to the charge of 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, demonstrating, or picketing in a Capitol Building. Ryan was sentenced to 60 days in prison, $500.00 restitution, and a $1,000.00 fine. Ryan, a Texas real estate broker flew on a private jet to attend the Capitol riot, and was arrested by Dallas FBI January 15, 2021. She was under investigation beginning when police found a trove of evidence online about her participation in the Jan. 6 pro-Trump riot. An FBI agent wrote in court papers that Ryan posted video footage of herself on board a private plane en route to the siege, explaining what she was prepared to do in Washington. Another video showed Ryan plug her realtor business as she and throngs of other Trump supporters stormed the Capitol building.

"Clifford Meteer left a stream of public comments on Facebook in the days following the U.S. Capitol riot, along with private messages to at least three people containing photos from inside the building, according to a criminal complaint. “I was one of those idiots scaling the wall,” he reportedly wrote to one friend, describing news coverage of the event as “extremely overblown.” “I saw no violence. I saw no destruction. Are you surprised he media is distorting reality?” he wrote in a public comment on Jan. 7, the complaint indicates. “I saw 2 kids trying to kick in a door and we told them to stop and they did. As to violence, I was right around the corner from the vet who was murdered.” Meteer’s relative and a former classmate both sent photos to the FBI in January, claiming they showed Meteer at the Jan. 6 riot, according to the complaint. The classmate told the FBI he’d seen several now-deleted posts of Meteer’s Facebook page, including a photo of Meteer holding up a sign reading “Save the republic.” The complaint alleges that video footage shows Meteer in various parts of the Capitol throughout a half-hour span." (NPR)

Name of case: United States of America v. Brent John Holdridge
Charges: 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building
Additional details: Resident of CA; "Holdridge Sentenced 1/9/23 to 60 Days Incarceration, 36 months Probation, Restitution $500, Special Assessment $10."
Short narrative: In July 2021, the FBI found that the cell phone belonging to Brent John Holdridge, 56, was detected within and outside the U.S. Capitol on January 6th. Holdridge was previously in custody in California for a drug-related offense and a probation violation, and a booking photo from the Humboldt County Jail was used to connect Holdridge to the riot in Washington D.C. earlier in the year. Footage from the U.S. Capitol surveillance system was compared with the booking photo and Holdridge was identified as one of the individuals who paraded about the interior and exterior of the United States Capitol on January 6. Holdridge's probation officer identified him in the footage from the U.S. Capitol during an interview; in an interview with Holdridge himself, he confirmed that he was at the U.S. Capitol that day, but refused to confirm if he did in fact make it inside the restricted building. Based on the aforementioned evidence, Holdridge was arrested and charged.

Short narrative: On August 30, 2023, in a superseding indictment, Derek Cooper Gunby, 43, of Anderson, South Carolina, was charged with numerous federal crimes for his actions at the U.S. Capitol on January 6, 2021. An Army veteran, Gunby traveled to D.C. to watch President Trump's rally at the Ellipse, and from there continued onward to the U.S. Capitol Building with the rest of the crowd. Gunby illegally entered the building through the Senate Parliamentarian Door, but was pushed out by law enforcement after about three minutes inside. Afterward, he moved about the other areas of the Capitol grounds and recorded the events going on there--including the fighting by the Lower West Terrace--on his phone. In fact, Gunby recorded most of his movements around D.C. with his phone, and images uploaded to his Facebook account later on were used by the FBI to identify him after he came to their attention.

Short narrative: On September 1, 2021, Pamela Anne Hemphill, 68, of Boise, Idaho was charged with multiple federal offenses for her activities at the United States Capitol on January 6, 2021. Hemphill was identified by the FBI through a tip that pointed them to numerous postings on her Facebook page and YouTube channel. A Facebook post of Hemphill's from December 28, 2020, read "It's not going to be a FUN Trump rally that is planned for January 6th, it's a WAR!" and another from January 1, 2021 announced that she was traveling to Washington, D.C. for the event, featuring a photo of her brandishing a large firearm. A YouTube video from Pam Hemphill showed footage taken at a January 5 event hosted by Alex Jones, with Hemphill in the background saying “Let’s do this; let’s go to the Capitol. We did it in Boise.” This remark was found to be in reference to the storming of a legislative session of the Idaho Legislature in August 2020, in which protestors raging against COVID-19 restrictions broke through a glass door at the Statehouse; Hemphill was determined to have participated in this event. On January 6, Hemphill slipped through the barricades set up outside the U.S. Capitol; when law enforcement ordered her to go back behind the barriers, she encouraged others to cross over with her. After the other rioters broke through, Hemphill was at the front of the line opposing the law enforcement officers. She entered the building through the East Rotunda, knowingly and illegally. After walking about the Rotunda for about ten minutes, Hemphill asked an officer to escort her out of the building, allegedly fearful that she would suffer an injury. Afterwards, Hemphill stayed outside the East Rotunda entrance, taking videos of the other rioters until the rest were dispersed.

He also appeared in a youtube video that was taken from inside the capitol. He fled to Ireland to try to escape his charges and voluntarily came back.

Name of case: United States of America v. Albert A. Ciarpelli
Charges: 18:1752(a)(1) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds with a Deadly or Dangerous Weapon Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds
Additional details: Syracuse, NY; "Albert Ciarpelli Sentenced 5/7/24 as to Count(s) 1, to Ninety (90) days incarceration followed by Twelve (12) months of Supervised Release and a Special Assessment of $25."
Short narrative: On November 14, 2023, Albert A. Ciarpelli, 65, of NY, was charged with and plead guilty to Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds for his participation in the U.S. Capitol riot on January 6, 2021. After travelling to Washington, D.C. to attend President Trump's "Stop the Steal' rally at the Ellipse, Ciarpelli proceeded to the U.S. Capitol Building with the crowd. He was one of the first rioters to breach the perimeter set up by USCP and ascended the stairs to the Upper West Terrace. After banging on the Parliamentarian's door and cheering on other protestors breaking glass along the building, he illegally entered it through the Senate Wing Door. While inside, Ciarpelli took videos and pictures and yelled at the police officers present in the building. Afterward, Ciarpelli's attorney contacted the USMS, who contacted the FBI, alerting them of Ciarpelli's presence at the riot and his illegal entrance into the Capitol building.

Name of case: United States of America v. Thomas Baranyi
Charges: 18:1752(a)(1) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building; 18:1752(a)(2) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building; 40:5104(e)(2)(D) Disorderly Conduct at the Grounds and in a Capitol Building; 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, and Picketing in a Capitol Building
Additional details: Resident of NJ; Sentenced 6/17/22 to 90 days in jail, one year of supervised release, 60 hours of community service and $500 restitution.
Short narrative: Thomas Baranyi, 28, is facing charges of entering a restricted building or grounds and violent entry. He was identified by an interview he gave after leaving the Capitol where he showed Ahsli Babbitt's blood on his hands. In a Facebook post, Baranyi’s father said his son graduated from the College of New Jersey, joined the Peace Corps, and also went into basic training for the U.S. Marine Corps but was discharged. While in the Peace Corps, he worked with a team of international volunteers in a government-led youth project from 2018 to 2019. After the Peace Corps, Baranyi enlisted in the Marine Corps, in July 2020, but left active duty before completing entry-level training on Parris Island in South Carolina.

Name of case: United States of America v. Robert Maurice Reeder
Charges: 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building
Additional details: Indicted by Bill of Information; Sentenced to 3 months imprisonment and $500 restitution
Short narrative: Robert Maurice Reeder was wearing a red Make America Great Again hat and chanted: "Fight for Trump" as he approached an open door in the Capitol. He's heard on the video asking an officer for water, with the officer directing him outside, the court record stated. But Reeder entered the building, and video captures him shouting at people not to destroy anything. Court documents indicate Reeder's video compilation showed he roamed around in the Capitol, possibly going out and back in again, for more than 90 minutes. At the end of the video, he recorded himself saying he'd been in for more than half an hour and had been gassed several times inside the building and many times outside. He has plead guilty to count four of his charges, parading, demonstrating, or picketing in a Capitol Building, allowing prosecutors to not prosecute on the further charges.

Name of case: United States of America v. Phillip Andrew Bromley
Charges: 18:1752(a)(2) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds
Additional details: Indicted by Bill of Information; Resident of AL; "Sentenced 6/28/22 to 90 days in jail, one year of supervised release, $2,000 restitution, $4,000 fine."
Short narrative: Phillip Andrew Bromley, 47, of Sterrett Alabama, was charged with Unlawful Entry to Restricted Building and Disorderly Conduct on Capitol Grounds related to his involvement in the January 6th attack on the Capitol. He was identified by federal agents in a video posted on Parler in which he identified himself and described how he entered the Capitol Building and witnessed the shooting of Ashli Babbitt.

Name of case: United States of America v. Jeffrey Alexander Smith
Charges: 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building
Additional details: Indicted by Bill of Information; Sentenced 3/15/22, 90 days of incarceration, 2 years of probation, $500 in restitution, 200 hours of community service.
Short narrative: "Following the events on January 6, 2021, the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) received tips at the FBI National Threat Operations Center (NTOC) from individuals who reported that they identified JEFFREY ALEXANDER SMITH, aka ALEX SMITH, as being involved in the events at the Capitol. On January 7, 2021, one individual (“Witness-1”) who identified themselves and who has known SMITH for an extended period of time had discovered a photo of SMITH inside the Capitol on social media which had been posted to Instagram by @homegrownterrorists. The photo depicts SMITH wearing a black jacket and a Trump hat, with a red cell phone in his right hand which is raised in the air. On January 8, 2021, a tip was received by the FBI Tipline from an individual (“Witness- 2”) who grew up with SMITH in Coronado, California, and who texted with SMITH via Instagram after the riots. Witness-2 provided screen shots of the messages which included SMITH writing, “I’m a Patriot”, “I stormed the capitol” (sic). In the text, SMITH stated that his purpose was “To send a message that Americans are[n’] t going to take a fraudulent election.” SMITH also wrote to Witness-2, “There is no way in hell I was going to drive 38 hours from San Diego and not walk right through the front of the capitol (sic) building.” Witness-2 also observed that SMITH had since deleted his Instagram account...SMITH told the [FBI] agent that he drove 38 hours to Washington, DC, to attend the speech by President Trump on January 6, 2021. SMITH said that his girlfriend traveled by air and met him in Washington, D.C. SMITH told his girlfriend to remain at the hotel instead of getting into all the chaos at the U.S. Capitol. SMITH also identified the hotel he stayed at in Washington, D.C. SMITH admitted that when he approached the U.S. Capitol it was a chaotic scene. He heard people on loudspeakers, he saw tear gas, and heard what he thought were flash bangs going off. SMITH admitted he walked into the Capitol on January 6, 2021 and remained in the Capitol for about 30 minutes. SMITH admitted to deleting his Instagram account after he began receiving threats related to his involvement in the Capitol events." (DOJ Statement of Facts) Smith was an Army Sergeant and was seen moving the bench barricades from the rotunda doors.

Name of case: United States of America v. Jason Riddle
Charges: 18:641 Theft of government property; 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building
Additional details: Resident of NH; US army Reserves Motor Transport Operator 2011-2016; Indicted by Bill of Information; Sentenced 4/4/22, 90 days in jail, followed by three years of probation, including 60 hours of community service, restitution of $754.
Short narrative: Jason Riddle, 32, has been arrested and charged for this role in the Capitol protests on January 6th, 2021. When he arrived to the Capitol, he drank a glass of wine from a bottle he found in a refrigerator in the Office of the Senate Parliamentarian and took a selfie with the bottle. He stated in a later interview that he was a military veteran. While Riddle was in the Capitol, he told the FBI he took two things, a small FOX News football and an old-looking, reddish-brown leather book from the same office where he found the wine. He then sold the book outside the Capitol for $40. "At some point, Riddle tried to delete messages, photos and videos from his phone, but the FBI was able to recover the digital evidence and found a photo of the book, titled "Senate Procedure." (USA Today)

Name of case: United States of America v. Derrick Evans
Charges: 18:231(a)(3) Civil Disorder
Additional details: Resident of WV; Indicted by a Bill of Information; Sentenced 6/22/22 to three months in jail, three years of supervised release, $2,000 fine, $2,000 restitution.
Short narrative: Derrick Evans, 35 of West Virginia, plead guilty to Impeding, Obstructing or Interfering with Law Enforcement During a Civil Disorder for his role in the January 6 Capitol riot. He was sentenced to 3 months in prison. During the event, the West Virginia Delegate live streamed footage of himself entering the Capitol building in Washington DC. Evans, a newly elected state representative from West Virginia, reportedly deleted the video soon after the siege ended, but it soon re-emerged on Reddit. Days later, Evans resigned from his office in the House of Delegates.

Name of case: United States of America v. James Bonet

Name of case: United States of America v. Kelly McFadden O'Brien
Charges: 18:1752(a)(1) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds; *18:1752(a)(2) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds; *40:5104(e)(2)(D) Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building; 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building;
Additional details: Resident of PA; Indicted by a Bill of Information; Sentenced 4/6/22 to 90 days of incarceration, 12 months of supervised release, $500 restitution, $1,000 fine; Expressed support for QAnon
Short narrative: Kelly O'Brien, 49, a resident of Pennsylvania, plead guilty to Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building for his role in the Capitol Raid. "A witness called the FBI after seeing videos on Kelly McFadden O'Brien's Facebook page reportedly showing her inside and nearby the U.S. Capitol on Jan. 6, 2021. In the videos, she narrates her path to the Capitol, reportedly saying: “We’re getting gassed and rubber bullets. We’re under Joe fake Biden Inaugural steps that he was supposed to be the fake president in. we’re probably about 20 feet to 40 feet from the Capitol doors. Some really brave patriots here. I’m right in the thick of it, following them up.” Law enforcement also identified O'Brien in security camera footage from inside the Capitol building on Jan. 6, 2021, court documents indicate. In social media posts leading up to Jan. 6, 2021, O'Brien reportedly posted often about what she believed was a stolen election, a claim for which there is no basis. On Nov. 26, 2020, she allegedly wrote: "We are an Army of Patriots. You will know us when you see us. There will be no ambiguity. Prepare yourself.” On Dec. 12, 2020, she allegedly posted about being in Washington, D.C., and said she was walked back to her hotel by the far-right extremist group the Proud Boys. A week later, she reportedly posted: "CALLING ALL PATRIOTS! Be in Washington D.C. January 6th. This wasn't organized by any group. DJT has invited us and it’s going to be 'wild.' " On Jan. 1, 2021, she made reference in a post to the "3 percent," which refers to a far-right extremist group named for the myth that only 3% of Colonists fought against the British during the American Revolution, court documents indicate, and in other posts she reportedly made references to QAnon. In a post on Jan. 7, 2021, O'Brien seemed to distance herself from those videos and posts that placed her among the Jan. 6, 2021, rioters, writing she “had to scrub my page, for obvious reasons,” according to court documents. Later, though, she reportedly wrote again: "No regrets" with a heart emoji." (NPR)

Name of case: United States of America v. Matthew Ryan Matulich
Charges: 18:641 Theft of government property
Additional details: Resident of Buras, Louisiana; Sentenced 9/5/24 to ninety (90) days incarceration, followed by nine (9) months of Supervised Release, a $25 Special Assessment, and Restitution in the amount of $500.

He illegally entered through the Senate Wing Door and spent about 40 minutes walking about the interior; while inside, he stole an American flag that he later brought home with him. Matulich was first identified through his cell records and later through Capitol video footage and an unidentified person.

Charges: 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building

I took this video. Capitol Police opened the doors, welcomed us in, and stood aside as we wandered the hallways. Is this what an insurrection looks like? Share this." After detecting her in these ways, the FBI spoke to Macandrew, who admitted to following the crowd to the Capitol and entering through the Senate Wing Door. Inside, she carried a Trump flag and filmed the events going on around her with her phone--videos that would later appear on Gab. Even after law enforcement officers ordered the rioters to leave, Macandrew stuck around by the Senate Wing Door and only actually left when they advanced upon her with riot shields.

Name of case: United States of America v. Richard Cook, et al.
Charges: 18:231(a)(3) Civil Disorder; *18:1752(a)(1) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds; *18:1752(a)(2) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds; *18:1752(a)(4) Engaging in Physical Violence in a Restricted Building or Grounds; *40:5104(e)(2)(E) Impeding Passage Through the Capitol Grounds or Buildings; *40:5104(e)(2)(F) Engage in an Act of Physical Violence in the Capitol Grounds or Buildings

Short narrative: On April 26, 2023, Arthur, 38, and Jessica, 38, Reyhers of Brownburg, Indiana, were charged with several felonies relating to the January 6th Capitol riot. The Reyhers repeatedly engaged in violent confrontations with law enforcement officers guarding the Capitol. Both of the Reyhers participated in collective pushes against police officers in the Lower West Terrace and tunnel areas in an attempt to gain access to the Capitol building. As stated by the DOJ, "[w]hile the Reyhers joined in collective pushes, one police officer screamed in pain as the weight of the rioters’ pushes pinned him between a shield and a door". The Reyhers returned to the tunnel multiple times to participate in these collective pushes against officers.

Name of case: United States of America v. Kenneth Rader
Charges: 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building
Verdict: Guilty on some charges/not guilty on others
Additional details: Resident of IA; Expressed support for QAnon; "Sentenced 9/29/22 to 90 days of incarceration, 36 months of probation, $500 restitution"
Short narrative: On February 18, 2022, Kenneth Bruce Rader, Jr., 53, of Sioux City, Iowa, was charged with illegally entering the U.S. Capitol Building during the riot that occurred there on January 6, 2021. He was identified by the FBI after one of his family members submitted a tip about him, pointing out his radicalization and social media postings that--among other things--threatened Vice President Mike Pence and President-elect Joe Biden. Further investigation of Rader's Facebook account indicated that he is an adherent of the QAnon conspiracy theory and that, after Joe Biden was declared the winner of the 2020 Presidential Election, he wrote that his certification would lead to blood being spilled in the streets. During an interview, Rader told FBI agents in September 2021 that he had attended the Jan. 6, 2021 rally and walked to the Capitol grounds after hearing a "boom." He told agents he looked inside the Capitol, but never entered. However, security footage shows Rader, dressed in a blue "Trump 2020" hoodie, entering the Capitol at 2:14 p.m. through the Senate wing door that had already been broken by protesters. A screen shot from the video shows Rader standing near the door. The video shows Rader enter the building, stand near a broken window, speak with several unidentified men and then exit. In an interview with the FBI, two of Rader's relatives identified him as the person shown and in a photo taken outside the Capitol.
