Name of case: United States of America v. Isaiah Farnsworth
Charges: 18:1361 Destruction of Government Property
Verdict: Guilty on some charges/not guilty on others
Additional details: Resident of CO; "Farnsworth Sentenced 9/8/23 to three months in prison and 36 months of supervised release for one felony count of destruction of government property."
Short narrative: On January 4, 2023, Isaiah Farnsworth, 44, of Broomfield, Colorado was charged for his actions at the United States Capitol on January 6, 2021. The FBI became aware of him after they received of tip that included a video of him boasting about his participation in the riot at a gathering. The FBI then looked into him and found images taken at the event on his Facebook page; also found there was a video dated January 6 in which a person believed to be Farnsworth can be heard saying "“We have a right to be at our house,” “We have a right to be on our lawn,” “We have a right to bring our grievances to the government,” and “Never, never be passive about such a powerful government any longer.” Other videos posted there further confirmed Farnsworth's presence at the U.S. Capitol on the day in question. Security footage from within the United States Capitol show the individual identified as Farnsworth entering the building and helping others to breach an interior door, breaking it. He then exited the U.S. Capitol through the same door he had entered through.

Name of case: United States of America v. Klein & Klein
Charges: 18:231(a)(3) Civil Disorder [2 counts]; 18:1752(a)(1) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds with a Deadly or Dangerous Weapon Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds
Verdict: Guilty on some charges/not guilty on others
Additional details: Resident of OR; Brother also arrested; Defendant remains on personal recognizance bond; Matthew Klein Sentenced 11/14/24 to 90 days in prison and 36 months of supervised release.
Short narrative: On March 23rd, 2021, Jonathanpeter Klein and his brother Matthew Leland Klein, both self-proclaimed members of the Proud Boys, were indicted on charges of 18:371 Conspiracy; 18:1512(c)(2), 2 Obstruction of an Official Proceeding and Aiding and Abetting; 18:231(a)(3), 2 Obstruction of Law Enforcement During Civil Disorder and Aiding and Abetting; 18:1361, 2 Destruction of Government Property and Aiding and Abetting; 18:1752(a)(1) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds; and 18:1752(a)(2) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds. Both pleaded not guilty to the charges, and their sentencing is pending. The Kleins came to the attention of law enforcement in fall 2020 when they attended Proud Boys rallies in Oregon. According to court records, Jonathanpeter Klein was seen at rallies in body armor and carrying a paintball gun, and was photographed shooting the paintball gun at "an unknown target." On Jan. 6, federal prosecutors allege, Matthew and Jonathanpeter Klein joined with the mob and other members of the Proud Boys to breach the Capitol. Once inside, prosecutors said, Jonathanpeter Klein was seen engaging in a "celebratory exchange" with another Proud Boys member and displayed a Proud Boys hand signal. After the initial breach, the men allegedly exited the building and then "joined together to wrench open a secure door on the Capitol’s north side," allowing more rioters to enter the building "as part of a second or third wave of attacks."

Name of case: United States of America v. Jamie N. Buteau, Jennifer Peck Buteau
Charges: 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building

Her husband is allegedly seen on footage from inside the Capitol assaulting two police officers by throwing a chair at them, and hitting one, as they were trying to move away from the rioters. Multiple tipsters, including a family member, contacted the FBI and reported that Buteau had posted live Facebook videos from within the building that she later deleted. “Antifa was infiltrating Trump supporters for the cameras, to cause Chaos,” Buteau allegedly wrote on Facebook. An additional tipster alerted the FBI that both Buteaus appeared in HBO’s Vice News Tonight report from August 2018 on QAnon believers. The FBI later confirmed that the video indeed featured the couple." (NPR)

Name of case: United States of America v. Ryan Scott Zink
Charges: 18:1752(a)(1) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds with a Deadly or Dangerous Weapon Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 18:1752(a)(2) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds
Verdict: Guilty on some charges/not guilty on others
Additional details: Son of congressional candidate Jeff Zink; resident of Lubbock, TX; "Ryan Scott Zink, 34, of Lubbock, Texas, was found guilty 9/13/23 after a jury trial in U.S. District Court. Zink was convicted of obstruction of an official proceeding and aiding and abetting, a felony offense, as well as two misdemeanor offense of entering and remaining in a restricted building or grounds and disorderly and disruptive conduct in a restricted building or grounds."
Short narrative: In 2021, Ryan Scott Zink, 32, of Lubbock, TX, son of congressional candidate, Jeff Zink, was charged with Obstruction of an Official Proceeding and Aiding and Abetting; Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds; Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds; Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building following his participation in the Capitol riot. Zink was identified via a tip provided to the FBI and subsequently numerous videos taken by Zink himself which clearly place Zink at the riot, and multiple Facebook posts from Zink detailing his experience in the Capitol. In one of the videos Zink says "We knocked down the gates! We're storming the Capitol! You can't stop us" (statement of facts). "Zink posted videos on Facebook discussing his participation in the riot, the FBI stated in court documents, including one in which he states: 'We knocked down the gates! We're storming the Capitol! You can't stop us.' He could also be heard in a video urging listeners to storm their own state capitols, the FBI stated. In a private message, documents show Zink stated: 'Broke down the doors, pushed Coungress out of session I took two flash bangs I'm ok I'll be posting pictures in a little bit when we get back I'm hurt but we accomplished the job'" (USA Today). Jeff Zink has articulated that he did not participate in the riot with his son. "ryan Zink Sentenced 9/20/24 to concurrent terms of three (3) months incarceration as to counts 2-3, followed by twelve (12) months of Supervised Release as to counts 2-3 to run concurrent, Special Assessments totaling $50, and Restitution in the amount of $500."

Name of case: United States of America v. Mick Chan
Charges: 18:1752(a)(1) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds with a Deadly or Dangerous Weapon Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 18:1752(a)(2) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building
Verdict: Guilty on some charges/not guilty on others
Additional details: Resident of NJ; Indicted by a Bill of Information; According to charging documents, Chan called FBI to blame riot on "Antifa and Black Lives Matter"; "Mick Chan Found guilty 1/24/23 as to Counts 1, 2, 4. Verdict of not guilty as to Count 3."
Short narrative: "On Jan. 7, a tipster reached out to the FBI to report that a friend had breached the U.S. Capitol with other people, including Mick Chan. That tipster provided a screenshot to the FBI of a Facebook post from a friend in which Chan was tagged, and which seemed to indicate that Chan and the friend had gotten massages after the Jan. 6 riot, court documents indicate. The post reportedly read: "After all the tear gas and rubber bullets shot at us, this massage today was like heaven on earth!" On Jan. 8, Chan contacted the FBI and allegedly admitted to entering the Capitol on Jan. 6. According to court documents, Chan told the FBI that he "broke into, well, air quotes, broke into" the Capitol and clarified that he believed others had breached the building before him. Chan reportedly told the FBI that he did not engage in any confrontations, believed the crowd had been infiltrated by antifa and Black Lives Matter and that he had entered the building with "journalistic intent." Chan also allegedly said he had previously met with members of the Proud Boys. In security camera footage from inside the Capitol, he is seen giving the middle finger to the camera, court documents indicate." (NPR)

Name of case: United States of America v. Eric J. Bochene
Charges: 18:1752(a)(1) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds with a Deadly or Dangerous Weapon Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds

Name of case: United States of America v. Wilmar Jeovanny Montano Alvarado
Charges: 18:231(a)(3) - Civil Disorder; 18:1512(c)(2), 2 - Obstruction of an Official Proceeding; 18:111(a)(1) - Assaulting, resisting, or impeding certain officers; 18:1752(a)(1) - Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 18:1752(a)(2) - Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a restricted Building or Grounds; 40:5104(e)(2)(D) - Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building; 40:5104(e)(2)(E) - Impeding Passage Through the Capitol Grounds or Buildings;
Additional details: Arrested by FBI in TX 1/29/21
Short narrative: On November 11th, 2021, Wilmar Jeovanny Montano Alvarado was charged via 2nd superseding indictment with Civil Disorder; Obstruction of an Official Proceeding; Assaulting, Resisting, or Impeding Certain Officers; Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds; Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds; Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building; Impeding Passage Through the Capitol Grounds or Buildings. According to the Houston Chronicle: "Jeovanny Montano Alvarado, a 37-year-old Salvadoran native and Houston resident, called the FBI on Jan. 14 to voluntarily identify himself as one of the people featured on an FBI flyer with photos of people suspected in the violent Capitol mob...He told the federal officials he did not go inside the Capitol building and did not assault any officers. Investigators reviewed a YouTube video of footage from the riot that they believe showed evidence "contrary" to Alvarado's voluntary statements, according to the criminal complaint. The Houston man "participated in efforts by rioters to violently battle their way through a line of police officers guarding the West Terrace entrance to the Capitol Building," the complaint alleges. In the video, Alvarado turns and pushes toward the police line with his arm extended and his hand on a police officer's shield at one point, officials said. The footage shows that Alvarado appears to get struck in the back of the head by an object from the mob and then "easily" makes his way out of the crowd. Two days after the riot and before boarding his flight back to Houston, Alvarado on Jan. 8 described his experience in a Zoom interview with a Fox 26 Houston reporter. He said he went to the Capitol to protest because he believed the election was fraudulent, according to the interview, but that he did not enter the building. The police presence was "almost non-existent," Alvarado told Fox 26, describing how he walked onto the Capitol grounds after people moved barriers aside. "I turned around trying to get out and it was really impossible because people kept pushing me in," he told the reporter. "I found myself really close to the cops. I was with my hands up and I told them, 'I’m not part of this. I’m trying to get out.'" Alvarado, who owns Betty's Bakery and Restaurant, is charged with violent entry or disorderly conduct; entering a restricted building or grounds; civil disorder; assaulting, resisting or impeding certain officers or employees; and obstruction of an official proceeding, according to a criminal complaint."

Short narrative: Law enforcement allegedly identified Isaiah Giddings as a person who participated in the Jan. 6, 2021, riot after searching the phone records of another person charged, Zachary Rehl, who is the president of the Philadelphia chapter of the Proud Boys, a far-right group. Giddings is charged with two other men, Brian Healion and Freedom Vy, who were allegedly part of a Telegram message group with Rehl and another person who was not in Washington, D.C., on the day of the insurrection. The group coordinated travel from Philadelphia to D.C. ahead of Jan. 6, 2021, and Giddings, Healion and Vy stayed together at The Darcy hotel in D.C. on the night before the riot, according to court records. On the day of the riot, Giddings allegedly appeared in a photograph outside the U.S. Capitol with Rehl and others, all flashing the "OK" hand symbol, a gesture associated with the Proud Boys. The four men then allegedly entered the Capitol building, where the four of them appear in several photos and videos. In a reply to a text the next day asking how they were doing, Giddings allegedly wrote: “Yes we have everything and everyone all accounted for ... none of our Philly guys had any PB gear the entire event just plain trump supporters from beginning to end." According to news reports, the Proud Boys were directed not to wear their signature black and yellow on the day of the riot, aiming to blend in with other Trump supporters. (NPR)

Additional details: "Mario Mares Found guilty at bench trial 10/31/24"
Short narrative: On January 6, 2021, Mario Mares, 50, participated in the Capitol Riot in Washington, DC. He entered and remained in a restricted building or grounds with a deadly or dangerous weapon and unlawfully possessed a firearm on Capitol grounds or in Capitol buildings.

Name of case: United States of America v. Chad Barrett Jones
Charges: 18:231(a)(3) and 2 Civil disorder and aiding and abetting; 18:1361 Destruction of government property exceeding $1,000; 18:1512(c)(2) and 2 Obstruction of an official proceeding and aiding and abetting; 18:1752(a)(1) and (b)(1)(A) Entering and remaining in a restricted building with a deadly or dangerous weapon; 18:1752(a)(2) and (b)(1)(A) Disorderly and disruptive conduct in a restricted building with a deadly or dangerous weapon; 18:1752(a)(4) and (b)(1)(A) Engaging in physical violence in a restricted building with a deadly or dangerous weapon; 40:5104(e)(2)(F) Act of physical violence in the Capitol building; 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, demonstrating, or picketing in Capitol
Additional details: Resident of Coxs Creek, KY; "Chad Jones Found guilty 7/26/23 of all nine charges against him following a bench trial."
Short narrative: Chad Barret Jones, 42, from Coxs Creek, Kentucky was charged for his role in the January 6, 2021 Capitol protests. A criminal affidavit describes video footage showing Jones in a red hooded jacket and gray skull cap from inside the capitol forcefully striking the glass door panels leading to the Speaker's Lobby at least 10 times with a long wood flagpole. A U.S. Capitol Police officer inside the Speaker's’ Lobby, facing the door with a gun raised, can be seenin the video in the close vicinity of the doorway. The window broken by Jones was the same window Ashli Babbitt tried to climb through before she was shot by Capitol police. The case is still pending. Jones has pleaded not guilty to all 9 charges.

Name of case: United States of America v. Samsel, et. al.
Charges: 18:231(a)(3), 2 Obstruction of Law Enforcement During Civil Disorder and Aiding and Abetting; 18:111(a)(1) and (b), 2 Assaulting, Resisting, or Impeding Certain Officers Using a Dangerous Weapon and Inflicting Bodily Injury on Certain Officers [2 counts]; 18:1752(a)(1) and (a)(1)(A) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds resulting in significant bodily injury; 18:1752(a)(2) and (b)(1)(A) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds with a Deadly or Dangerous Weapon; 18:1752(a)(4), (b)(1)(A), (b)(1)(B), 2 Engaging in Physical Violence in a Restricted Building or Grounds with a Deadly or Dangerous Weapon and Causing Significant Bodily Injury; 40:5104(e)(2)(D) Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building; 40:5104(e)(2)(F), 2 Act of Physical Violence in the Capitol Grounds or Building; 18:1512(c)(2) 2, Obstruction of an Official Proceeding and Aiding and Abetting; 18:231(a)(3) Civil Disorder; 18:111(a)(1) Assaulting, Resisting, or Impeding Certain Officers;
Additional details: Resident of PA; Bench trial verdict on 2/2/2024 finds him Guilty on eight charges; Sentencing set for 6/2024
Short narrative: Ryan Stephen Samsel, 37, of Bristol, Pennsylvania, was found guilty for his role in the Jan. 6th Capitol rios after helping dismantle barricades at the Capitol building and knocking over a U.S. Capitol Police Officer, who then suffered a concussion. Samsel was charged with one count of forcible assault/opposition or interference with a federal agent engaged in official duties, one count of committing or attempt to commit any act to obstruct, impede, or interfere with any firearm or law enforcement officer engaged in official duty, and one count of obstruction/impeding or attempt to, an official proceeding. He entered a plea of not guilty on 9/14/2021 and and was found guilty on 2/2/24 of civil disorder, assaulting an officer with a dangerous or deadly weapon, obstructing an official proceeding, assaulting, resisting, or impeding certain officers, and assaulting, resisting, or impeding certain officers using a dangerous weapon. He sentencing was on June 13, 2023.

Name of case: United States of America v. Vitali Gossjankowski
Charges: 18:231(a)(3) Civil Disorder; 18:1512(c)(2) and 2 Obstruction of an Official Proceeding; 18:111(a)(1) and (b) Assaulting, Resisting, or Impeding Certain Officers Using a Dangerous Weapon; 18:1752(a)(1) and (2) and (b)(1)(A) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds With a Deadly or Dangerous Weapon; 18:1752(a)(2) and (b)(1)(A) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds With a Deadly or Dangerous Weapon; 40:5104(e)(2)(D) Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building
Additional details: Turned himself in after finding out he was included on an FBI "wanted" poster. He admitted to possessing a Taser but told officers that he found it on the ground while walking toward to the Capitol.
Short narrative: On November 10, 2021, Vitali GossJankowski, a student attending Gallaudet University, was charged with 18:231(a)(3) Civil Disorder; 18:1512(c)(2) and 2 Obstruction of an Official Proceeding; 18:111(a)(1) and (b) Assaulting, Resisting, or Impeding Certain Officers Using a Dangerous Weapon; 18:1752(a)(1) and (2) and (b)(1)(A) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds With a Deadly or Dangerous Weapon; 18:1752(a)(2) and (b)(1)(A) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds With a Deadly or Dangerous Weapon; 40:5104(e)(2)(D) Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building via superseding indictment. Video shows GossJankowski carrying a police riot shield and holding a taser he claims he found on the floor of the Capitol. GossJankowski plead not guilty to all charges and sentencing information is pending.

Name of case: United States of America v. John Joseph Richter
Charges: 18:1512(c)(2), 2 Obstruction of an Official Proceeding and Aiding and Abetting; 18:1752(a)(1) and (b)(1)(A) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds with a Deadly or Dangerous Weapon; 18:1752(a)(2) and (b)(1)(A) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds with a Deadly or Dangerous Weapon; 40:5104(e)(2)(A) Entering and Remaining on the Floor of Congress; 40:5104(e)(2)(D) Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building; 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building
Additional details: Resident of FL ; "Found Guilty in a Bench trial on 5/14/2024 on four charges and two lesser charges. The court vacated the Obstruction conviction on 11/22/2024. Sentencing reset for 1/22/2025. On 1/21/2025, the court grants the government’s motion to dismiss the case with prejudice.
Short narrative: On February 17, 2023, John Joseph Richter, 38, of Port Charlotte, FL, was issued a complaint with several felony and misdemeanor charges relating to the January 6th Capitol riot. Richter was seen with his friend and co-offender, Joseph Irwin, illegally entering the Capitol building. While in the Capitol, Richter took pictures of rioters, the building, and himself sitting at the desks of senators. For the majority of Richter's time in the Capitol, he is seen holding a flag pole that he retrieved earlier during the riot. He was seen exiting the U.S. Capitol Building with this pole still in hand as one of the last rioters inside the building.

Name of case: United States of America v. Timothy Rowbottom
Charges: 18:1752(a)(1) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 18:1752(a)(2) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 40:5104(e)(2)(D) Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building or Grounds; 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building
Additional details: Resident of PA; Found Guilty on all charges in a Bench trial on 11/19/2024. Former Republican candidate for Harrisburg Mayor. Sentencing set for 2/14/2025 but pardoned before
Short narrative: On May 1, 2024, Timothy Rowbottom, 44, of Allison Hill, Pennsylvania, was indicted for his involvement in the January 6 Capitol riot. Pictures and information about Rowbottom's involvement in the Capitol riot were sent to the FBI and matched his driver's license photo and additional CCTV footage. He entered the Capitol through the Senate Wing door and walked through the Rotunda, staying inside the building for about forty minutes. He was interviewed by an FBI investigator and admitted to being present inside the building on January 6. He was pardoned by President Trump before he could be sentenced for his guilty charges.

Name of case: United States of America v. Johnson, et al.
Charges: 18:231(a)(3) and 2 Civil Disorder; 18:1752(a)(1) and 2 Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 18:1752(a)(2) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 40:5104(e)(2)(D) Disorderly Conduct in the Capitol Grounds or Buildings
Additional details: Resident of Coldwater, FL; James Brett IV was found guilty on 11/19/24 at the bench trial, convicted of the civil disorder charge after pleading guilty to the other three; he was pardoned before sentencing
Short narrative: On May 25, 2022, James Brett, IV of Florida was indicted alongside four others for his involvement in the Capitol riot. He was part of a group that illegally entered Capitol grounds and moved to the Lower West Terrace, where rioters clashed with police.  According to the DOJ, at approximately 12:53 p.m., Brett and other defendants first breached the restricted area near the Peace Circle and advanced. By approximately 12:58 p.m., Brett reached a barricade on the Lower West Plaza and pushed past law enforcement. Brett joined the toppling of a permanent barricade before jumping over and helping others cross. Brett then advanced with the mob to the West Plaza, where tension between rioters and the police became physical and Brett remained nearby. Rioters, including Brett at 3:15 p.m., followed police into the Tunnel until he was forced out by police a few minutes later. Brett stayed near the Tunnel's entrance until an officer pushed him away. As he descended the stairs to leave, Brett passed close to two police officers who had been violently dragged into the crowd by rioters. His relationship to his co-defendants is still unclear.

Name of case: United States of America v. Cook, et al.
Charges: 18:231(a)(3) Civil Disorder; 18:1752(a)(1) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 18:1752(a)(2) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 18:1752(a)(4) Engaging in Physical Violence in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 40:5104(e)(2)(E) Impeding Passage Through the Capitol Grounds or Buildings; 40:5104(e)(2)(F) Act of Physical Violence in the Capitol Grounds or Building;
Additional details: Resident of Gun Barrel City, TX; "William Sarsfield Found guilty 11/1/24 at jury trial," Pardoned before sentencing could occur
Short narrative: On April 24, 2023, William Patrick Sarsfield, 46 of Texas, was charged with several offenses for his involvement in the January 6 Capitol riot. He was among rioters who repeatedly engaged in violence against law enforcement officers guarding the Capitol. "Sarsfield participated in the confrontation with law enforcement officers in the Lower West Terrace and tunnel areas of the Capitol. He entered the tunnel on the Lower West Terrace at approximately 3:12 p.m., making his way into the mob of rioters who were coordinating pushes against police officers while yelling “HEAVE HO!” and “PUSH!” Sarsfield entered the tunnel three separate times to assist in the collective pushes against police officers as the rioters tried to gain access to the Capitol building. While Sarsfield joined in collective pushes, one police officer screamed in pain as the weight of the rioters’ pushes pinned him between a shield and a door. Sarsfield also assisted in passing stolen police shields into the tunnel." (DOJ Press Release)

Charges: 18:1512(c)(2), 2 Obstruction of an Official Proceeding; 18:1752(a)(1) and (b)(1)(A) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds with a Deadly or Dangerous Weapon; 18:1752(a)(2) and (b)(1)(A) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds with a Deadly or Dangerous Weapon; 40:5104(e)(2)(A) Entering and Remaining on the Floor of Congress; 40:5104(e)(2)(D) Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building; 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building

Sentencing reset for 1/22/2025. On 1/21/2025, the court granted the government’s motion to dismiss the case with prejudice.
Short narrative: On January 11, 2023 Joseph Irwin, 42, of Cecilia, KY, was charged with multiple federal crimes in a superseding indictment for his role in the January 2021 Capitol protests. Irwin and his friend, John Joseph Richter, planned, prepared, and traveled to the Capitol together to attend the Stop the Steal rally and then the Capitol riot. They were some of the last rioters to remain in the Capitol building.

Name of case: United States of America v. Brian Glenn Bingham
Charges: 18:231(a)(3) Civil Disorder; 18:111(a)(1) Assaulting, Resisting, or Impeding Certain Officers; 18:1752(a)(1) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 18:1752(a)(2) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 40:5104(e)(2)(D) Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building; 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating or Picketing in a Capitol Building
Additional details: Resident of FL; found guilty of all charges by trial on 11/4/24; Sentencing set for 2/7/2025. On 1/21/2025, the court granted the government’s motion to dismiss the case with prejudice.
Short narrative: On March 18, 2022, Brian Glenn Bingham, 36, from Port Charlotte, Florida, was charged with several federal offenses for his involvement in the January 6 Capitol riot. While inside the Capitol, he pushed and grabbed an officer after yelling at nearby police.  The police officer was trying to coax Bingham out of the Capitol. "Footage from surveillance cameras and police body cameras allegedly show Bingham appearing "to throw a punch or a shove at the officer with his right arm" and scratching the officer's eye before other officers pulled him away and Bingham eventually left the building. Prosecutors cite a Facebook message Bingham allegedly sent later that day: "I got to manhandle] 5 cops and live to tell.". He was arrested on June 23, 2021. He has ties to Florida and New Jersey." (NPR)

Name of case: United States of America v. Joseph Julius Lapoint, et. al.
Charges: 18:1752(a)(1) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 18:1752(a)(2) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 40:5104(e)(2)(D) Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building; 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building;
Additional details: Resident of FL
Short narrative: "According to court documents, a tipster informed the FBI that their relative, Joseph Lapoint, had entered the Capitol on Jan. 6, 2021, and posted a photo of himself on social media, standing on a window ledge inside one of the offices. The tipster also referenced videos that show him with his girlfriend or fiancé, Nicole Joyner. On Jan. 6, 2022, court documents state, Lapoint posted a video of himself and Joyner on his TikTok account with the text “HAD A BLAST one year ago” and “me and babe stormed the Capitol with the rest of America.” Lapoint first appeared in federal court on March 12, 2024" (NPR)

Name of case: United States of America v. Amy Nicole Gordon
Charges: 18:1752(a)(1) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 18:1752(a)(2) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 40:5104(e)(2)(D) Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building or Grounds; 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building
Additional details: Resident of Greenville, IN; Found guilty by jury on all counts, but pardoned by President Trump before sentencing could take place
Short narrative: On April 16, 2024, Amy Nicole Gordon, 40, of Greenville, IN was charged with numerous federal crimes for her actions during the January 6, 2021 Capitol riot. According to court documents, Gordon was identified through images captured on the west side of the Capitol Building exterior, which showed her carrying an American Flag with an eagle attached to the end of the pole. Additional images show that Gordon illegally entered the U.S. Capitol Building with an unidentified male through the Senate Wing Door. Gordon was inside the building for about nine minutes before leaving through the same entrance. Interviews with Gordon herself and others reveal that she travelled from Greenville, IN to Washington, D.C. with the unidentified male and others, as part of a group known as the Southern Indiana Patriots.

Name of case: United States of America v. Ryan Wilson
Charges: 18:231(a)(3) Civil Disorder; 18:111(a)(1) Assaulting, Resisting, or Impeding Certain Officers; 18:111(a)(1) and (b) Assaulting, Resisting, or Impeding Certain Officers Using a Dangerous Weapon; 18:1752(a)(1) and (b)(1)(A) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds with a Deadly or Dangerous Weapon; 18:1752(a)(2) and (b)(1)(A) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds with a Deadly or Dangerous Weapon; 18:1752(a)(4) and (b)(1)(A) Impeding Passage Through the Capitol Grounds or Buildings with a Deadly or Dangerous Weapon); 40:5104(e)(2)(D) Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building; 40:5104(e)(2)(F) Act of Physical Violence in the Capitol Grounds or Buildings
Additional details: Resident of Athena, Oregon; pardoned by President Trump before sentencing could occur
Short narrative: On October 4, 2024, Ryan Wilson, 40, of Athena, Oregon, was charged with numerous federal crimes stemming from his actions at the U.S. Capitol on January 6, 2021. According to court documents, Wilson traveled to Washington, D.C. and participated in the riot with his father. Video footage depicts Wilson throwing a water bottle toward the police line during riots in the Lower West Terrace Tunnel of the United States Capitol. Wilson then grabs a pipe from another rioter and rammed it toward the police. After a policeman sprayed Wilson with OC spray, Wilson threw the pipe toward the police line and then exited the tunnel.

Name of case: United States of America v. Thomas Paul Osborne
Charges: 18:231(a)(3) Civil Disorder; 18:1752(a)(1) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 18:1752(a)(2): Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 40:5104(e)(2)(D) Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building;
Additional details: Resident of Lakeland, Florida; found guilty of all charges on December 5, 2024; pardoned by President Trump before sentencing could occur
Short narrative: On February 21, 2024, Thomas Paul Osborne, 40, of Lakeland, Florida, was charged with numerous federal offenses stemming from his involvement in the January 6, 2021 Insurrection. While encroaching upon the U.S. Capitol, Osborne grabbed the baton of a law enforcement officer as he was defending the building. Osborne apparently traveled to Washington, D.C. with the owners of the gun shop he worked at, fellow Lakeland residents Jonathan and Olivia Pollock; the siblings went into hiding after the event. Furthermore, Osborne is believed to have harbored Christopher Worrell, a Proud Boy who also went on the run after storming the U.S. Capitol. Several of Worrell's belongings were found in Osborne's home during the FBI's search.

Name of case: United States of America v. David Allan Davis
Charges: *18:1512(c)(2), 2 Obstruction of an Official Proceeding; 18:1752(a)(1) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 18:1752(a)(2) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 40:5104(e)(2)(D) Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building; 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in the Capitol Building
Additional details: Resident of Keller, TX; pardoned by President Trump before sentencing
Short narrative: On October 11, 2023, David Allan Davis, of Keller, TX was charged with numerous federal offenses following his participation in the riot at the U.S. Capitol on January 6, 2021. Davis was identified via an anonymous tip, photographs, CCTV footage, and extensive tweets from his Twitter account. According to court documents, Davis illegally entered the U.S. Capitol Building through the Senate Wing Door. From there, he proceeded to the Crypt, where he was seen on video footage chanting "lock them up!" with the other rioters. There, Davis was near the front of the crowd that rushed a line of police officers as it moved forward through the Memorial Door. Davis then went up to Statuary Hall and followed the crowd as they pushed past officers to go to the hallway outside the House Main Door. Around this time, Davis also entered the Rayburn Reception Room twice. He then exited the building through the East House Front Door, after spending about thirty-nine minutes inside the building.

Name of case: United States of America v. Deborah Lynn Lee
Charges: 18:1752(a)(1) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 18:1752(a)(2) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 40:5104(e)(2)(D) Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building; 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building
Additional details: Resident of PA; On 8/2/2024, the court granted the motion to dismiss Count 1, Obstruction. Found Guilty on all charges on 10/11/2024. Sentencing set for 1/27/2025. On 1/21/2025, the court grants the government’s motion to dismiss the case with prejudice.
Short narrative: On August 27, 2021, Deborah Lynn Lee, 55, of PA, was indicted with several charges following her participation in the January 6 Capitol riot. Lee was identified via photos and posts made to her Facebook account from inside the Capitol. On Facebook, she said "ITS OUR HOUSE. F*** NANCY AND THE DEMOCRATS. WE HAVE EVERY RIGHT TO OCCUPY OUR CAPITAL!! [sic]" "According to court documents, she claimed that antifa was there and that she and others took weapons from the anti-fascist groups, though there is no evidence that such groups played any major part in the riot. Security camera footage also placed Lee in the Capitol that day, court documents indicate." (NPR)

Name of case: United States of America v. Lawrence Silas Billiter
Charges: 18:231(a)(3) Civil Disorder; 18:1512(c)(2), 2 Obstruction of an Official Proceeding; 18:111(a)(1) and (b) Assaulting, Resisting, or Impeding Certain Officers Using a Deadly or Dangerous Weapon; 18:111(a)(1), 2 Assaulting, Resisting, or Impeding Certain Officers; 18:1752(a)(1) and (b)(1)(A) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds With a Deadly or Dangerous Weapon; 18:1752(a)(2) and (b)(1)(A) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds With a Deadly or Dangerous Weapon; 18:1752(a)(4) and (b)(1)(A) Engaging in Physical Violence in a Restricted Building or Grounds With a Deadly or Dangerous Weapon; 40:5104(e)(2)(D) Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building; 40:5104(e)(2)(F) Act of Physical Violence in the Capitol Grounds or Buildings; 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating or Picketing in a Capitol Building
Verdict: Guilty on some charges/not guilty on others
Additional details: Resident of Flint, Michigan (DOJ); "For the reasons stated on the record, the Court finds the Defendant GUILTY as to Counts 1, 4, 8, 9, and 10 of the 12 Indictment. Additionally, the Court finds the Defendant GUILTY as to the lesser included offenses of Counts 3, 5, 6, and 7 of the 12 Indictment."
Short narrative: On November 29, 2023, Lawrence Silas Billiter, 30, was charged with numerous federal crimes for his actions at the U.S. Capitol. According to court documents, Billiter claimed to have traveled from North Dakota "armed with enough ammo too [sic] win a small war"--according to his posts on "thedonald.win." Footage from the insurrection captured Billiter approaching a line of police officers, pulled a bike rack away from one such officer, strike the rack with a metal pole, and then throw the pole at an officer. After this altercation, he was pepper-sprayed. He illegally entered the U.S. Capitol Building through the Senate Parliamentarian Door; he was inside for only two minutes, during which time he joined the mob in surging towards the officers near the broken doors. He made a second illegal entrance through the Senate Wing Door and briefly milled about the interior before exiting again. Thereafter, he stayed on the Capitol grounds for about an hour and a half before being dispelled by law enforcement. He was identified by the FBI through his posts on thedonald.win.

Name of case: United States of America v. Jerry Daniel Braun
Charges: 18:231(a)(3) Civil Disorder; *18:1512(c)(2), 2 Obstruction of an Official Proceeding; 18:111(a)(1) Assaulting, Resisting, or Impeding Certain Officers; 18:111(a)(1) and (b) Assaulting, Resisting, or Impeding Certain Officers Using a Dangerous Weapon; *18:1361 Destruction of Government Property; 18:1752(a)(1) and (b)(1)(A) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds With a Deadly or Dangerous Weapon; 18:1752(a)(2) and (b)(1)(A) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds with a Deadly or Dangerous Weapon; 18:1752(a)(4) and (b)(1)(A) Engaging in Physical Violence in a Restricted Building or Grounds with a Deadly or Dangerous Weapon; 40:5104(e)(2)(D) Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building; 40:5104(e)(2)(F) Act of Physical Violence in the Capitol Grounds or Building
Verdict: Guilty on some charges/not guilty on others
Additional details: Resident of CA; "Plea Hearing as to JERRY DANIEL BRAUN held on 10/8/2024. Plea of GUILTY entered as to Counts 1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10." "On 10/2/2024, the court dismissed counts 2 and 5: Obstruction and Destruction of Gov't Property." Pardoned by President Trump before sentencing could take place.
Short narrative: On October 4, 2024, Jerry Daniel Braun, 69, was charged with numerous federal offenses stemming from his actions at the United States Capitol on January 6, 2021. According to court documents, Braun encroached upon the U.S. Capitol Building's West Plaza restricted area with the rest of the mob of rioters that went there after President Trump's speech at the Ellipse. There, Braun joined the mob in resisting law enforcement's efforts to repel them. He swung a cane at several people and shouted "Fuck you, traitor!" at police. Braun also tried to wrestle a bike rack being used as a barricade away from several officers. He then picked up a wooden beam and jabbed at the police with it. Braun used the beam to strike a person in a "PRESS" helmet holding a camera; he also swatted at them with his hand. After this commotion, Braun remained within the Capitol perimeter for several more hours; he was believed to be on the grounds until 4:00 PM. Braun was identified after an his Uber driver tipped him off to the FBI, saying that he bragged about his participation in the riot and his injury while in the car.

Name of case: United States of America v. Mitchell Bosch
Charges: 18:231(a)(3) Civil Disorder; 18:111(a)(1) Assaulting, Resisting, or Impeding Certain Officers; 18:1752(a)(1) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 18:1752(a)(2) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds; *18:1752(a)(4) Engaging in Physical Violence in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 40:5104(e)(2)(D) Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building; 40:5104(e)(2)(F) Act of Physical Violence in the Capitol Grounds or Buildings
Verdict: Guilty on some charges/not guilty on others
Additional details: Resident of NY; Bosch was also arrested at an anti-vax protest at the New York Museum of Natural History; "Jury found defendant guilty on counts 1,2,3,4,6,7 and found defendant not guilty on count 5. Sentencing is scheduled for April 14, 2025"
Short narrative: On May 1, 2024, Mitchell Bosch, 44, of Brooklyn, NY was charged with numerous federal offenses stemming from his actions at the U.S. Capitol on January 6, 2021. According to court documents, Bosch was captured in video footage fighting with law enforcement officers on the U.S. Capitol Building's Northwest Courtyard. In several instances, Bosch helped other rioters in their attempts to push against the  police advance; in others, he was at the front of the mob directly pushing against the police and their riot shields. Bosch encouraged other rioters to do the same, shouting "hold the line" and joining them in chanting "USA!" After being repelled, Bosch rushed the police line again before falling back amidst the crowd. They joined in the mass effort to push against a line of law enforcement officers at the bottom of a short flight of stairs. Martin, however, retreated after he was pepper sprayed directly in the face. Martin first came to the attention of the FBI when several concerned citizens submitted tips that included photos and Facebook posts of Martin at the riot. During the investigation the FBI received a search warrant for his Facebook account where they found a significant amount of content related to the 2020 Presidential Election, such as several messages and images about the election being stolen.

Name of case: United States of America v. Patrick Duffy
Charges: 18:1752(a)(1) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 18:1752(a)(2) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 40:5104(e)(2)(D) Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building; 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building
Additional details: Resident of Cleveland Heights, OH
Short narrative: "Court documents allege that on Jan. 6, 2021, Patrick Duffy of Cleveland Heights, Ohio, made his way from the White House Ellipse down Pennsylvania Avenue toward the U.S. Capitol building at approximately 1 pm. Open-source video showed Duffy in the crowd walking directly behind right-wing provocateur Alex Jones during that time. As protestors reached the east side of the Capitol building, Duffy joined a group that took a riot shield from a police officer and pushed through an entrance guarded by police. He entered the building at around 2:45 pm, making his way through the Rotunda and a hallway outside the Old Senate Chambers. He was arrested on Mar. 6, 2024, in Cleveland, Ohio." (NPR)

Additional details: Resident of Summit, IL; pardoned
Short narrative: "According to court documents, shortly after 2:30 pm on Jan. 6, 2021, John Banuelos climbed a scaffolding outside the U.S. Capitol building, pulled a gun out of his waistband and fired two shots into the sky. Banuelos was seen in open-source video and body-worn camera footage throughout the afternoon on Capitol grounds wearing a red puffy jacket, black boots and knee pads, and a white "Trump 2020" cowboy hat. Federal investigators first became aware of Banuelos' actions that afternoon in 2021; he was arrested on Mar. 8, 2024, in Summit, Ill." (NPR)

Short narrative: "The FBI reviewed many social media posts showing Charles Espinosa on January 6, 2021, known by the Instagram username “Charlie_alpha_echo,” court documents state. One video tagging that account showed Espinosa on the steps of the Capitol, speaking to the crowd through a megaphone held by another rioter, saying, “I think this should be happening in every single major city in the country.” Espinosa’s previous employer provided his attendance records to the FBI, showing he requested paid time off for January 6 and 7, 2021. Court documents state that he entered the Capitol building around 2:14 pm and exited 45 minutes later. He was arrested Mar. 26, 2024 in Derry, NH." (NRP)

Name of case: United States of America v. Zeis & Schulze
Charges: 18:1752(a)(1) Entering and Remaining in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 18:1752(a)(2) Disorderly and Disruptive Conduct in a Restricted Building or Grounds; 18:231(a)(3) Obstruction of Law Enforcement During Civil Disorder; 40:5104 (e)(2)(D) Disorderly Conduct in a Capitol Building; 40:5104(e)(2)(G) Parading, Demonstrating, or Picketing in a Capitol Building
Additional details: Resident of Monument, Colorado; Attended the "Stop the Steal" Rally before arriving at the Capitol; Was considered the leader of the group that traveled to Washington D.C. to attend President Trump's speech at the rally mentioned prior.
Short narrative: On November 13, 2023, Eric D. Zeis, along with Justin R. Schulze, were charged in the District of Columbia for allegedly "obstructing] law enforcement during civil disorder. In addition to the felony, the two [were] charged with several misdemeanor offenses, including disorderly and disruptive conduct in a restricted building or grounds, disorderly conduct in a Capitol building, and parading, demonstrating, or picketing in a Capitol building" (DOJ). On January 6, 2021, Zeis and Schulze "joined a large group that forced officers from the United States Capitol Police (USCP) to retreat to the East Rotunda doors" (United States of America v. Eric Zeis, Statement of Facts). After entering the Capitol, Zeis and Schulze "made their way to varying parts of the Capitol" (United States of America v. Eric Zeis, Statement of Facts). After making their way to the Statuary Hall Connector, "they immersed themselves in a larger group confronting officers guarding the U.S. House of Representatives chambers...Zeis and Schulze eventually retraced their steps back throughout the Capitol stopping in the Rotunda. Zeis is seen, in an open-source video, joining a group who collectively pushed officers...after shoving forward, Zeis turned around and called 'Justin'...Schulze then joined the group pushing against the officers;" then, Zeis and Schulze exited the Capitol through the Rotunda Door (United States of America v. Eric Zeis, Statement of Facts).

Short narrative: On January 18, 2024, Justin LaGesse and Theodore Middendorf, of McLeansboro, Illinois, were "charged in a criminal complaint filed in the District of Columbia with felony destruction of property. In addition to the felony, LaGesse and Middendorf are charged with misdemeanor offenses of entering and remaining in a restricted building or grounds, disorderly and disruptive conduct in a restricted building or grounds, engaging in physical violence in a restricted building or grounds, disorderly conduct in a Capitol building, act of physical violence in the Capitol grounds or building, and parading, picketing, and demonstrating in a Capitol building" (DOJ Press Release). On January 6, 2021, LaGeese entered the U.S. Capitol Building through a broken window "next to the Senate Wing Door" with a Gadsden and America flag, then helps Middendorf through the same window (Charging Documents; Statement of Facts). They then entered the Crypt and "continued south into the House of Representatives side of the U.S. Capitol" (Charging Documents; Statement of Facts). They passed the House Wind Door emergency exit and "continued south through the Hall of Columns" before leaving the Capitol through the South Door (Charging Documents; Statement of Facts). They then approached MPD officers and LaGesse verbally insulted them while Middendorf stood nearby (Charging Documents; Statement of Facts). Afterward, as they approached a group of rioters attempting to breach the North Doors, they "used their flagpoles to strike the window numerous times and damaged the window in several places" (Charging Document; Statement of Facts). Middendorf proceeded to strike another window with his flagpole once. The damage from both men amounted to $41,315.25.

Additional details: Resident of IL
Short narrative: Federal prosecutors say that Roy Franklin was one of the rioters that made his way to the Senate floor on the day of the riot at the U.S. Capitol. Court documents indicate that Franklin traveled to Washington, D.C., with his friend Thomas Adams Jr., who was charged in April of 2021. The criminal complaint references an article from *Insider,* published the day after the riot, that says Franklin tripped while at the bottom of the Capitol steps and fell onto an officer who he says “barely reacted.” The article reported that Franklin followed a group of people who were climbing scaffolding and entering the building through a window that was smashed. Once inside, Franklin allegedly followed people onto the floor of the Senate and observed “a shirtless man with an animal skin headdress and his face painted red, white, and blue stood at the speaker's chair, wielding a bullhorn, and flexing his biceps” who was presumably Jacob Chansley, also known as the QAnon Shaman. Months after the riot, agents say they tracked Franklin down at his house, executed a search warrant and seized gear that they claim can be seen in images of that day and in particular the footage from the Senate floor: a Trump 2020 Keep America Great flag, a plaid patterned shirt, a pair of Nike shoes and a baseball cap emblazoned with “United States of America” and a flag in the center. During the execution of the search warrant, an FBI agent alleges that he overheard a conversation between Franklin and his significant other. In the conversation, Franklin allegedly admitted that he was in the Capitol building. He also allegedly said, “You had to be there, the whole thing was fun.” (NPR)

Additional details: Resident of FL; Identified through comparison of defendant's ear
Short narrative: James Beeks was allegedly part of a group of Oath Keepers members and affiliates that marched on the U.S Capitol on Jan. 6, 2021. Prosecutors say that he was already on the radar of law enforcement after a rioter who pleaded guilty identified him as one of the people who lined up with the Oath Keepers the day of the riot. The criminal complaint alleges that he was part of the group that entered into a formation — called a “stack” — in order to force its way into the Capitol. Court documents enumerate many records obtained that show Beeks traveled to Washington, D.C., on the day of the riot, including records from a personal finance app and a rental car agency, as well as cell phone records. Beeks was not wearing the typical camouflage favored by the far-right extremist group, according to court documents, but instead appears in images from that day in a black jacket with the word “Bad” on it in red letters, from Michael Jackson's 1987 world tour. It is that jacket that helped lead law enforcement to him; agents found photographs on Instagram of a person who appears to be Beeks wearing the jacket while posing in front of a sign for the musical play Jesus Christ Superstar. Beeks is an actor who performs as Judas — under the stage name James T. Justis — in the traveling production of the play, and the criminal complaint notes he was observed performing the role in both San Francisco and Los Angeles. In addition, he has also performed as a Michael Jackson impersonator. Prosecutors claim that Beeks changed his phone and phone number the day after an indictment naming co-conspirators was filed and registered his new phone under his stage name. After Beeks was charged, he appeared in court and claimed that the U.S. government had no authority over him — which a U.S. District judge called “gobbledygook.” The production of Jesus Christ Superstar has since replaced him in the role of Judas. (NPR)

Short narrative: Federal prosecutors allege that James Haffner took part in the U.S. Capitol riot along with another man from the Seattle area named Ronald Loehrke. According to documents filed in federal court, Loehrke communicated in December 2020 with Ethan Nordean, a leader of the extremist group the Proud Boys who is facing conspiracy charges connected to the Jan. 6, 2021, attack. Nordean allegedly told Loehrke that he wanted Loehrke "on the front line" with him on Jan. 6, 2021. Loehrke allegedly agreed and said he was bringing three "Bad mother f******" with him to Washington, D.C. On the day of the attack, prosecutors say, Haffner and Loehrke marched with members and associates of the Proud Boys toward the Capitol. They then allegedly dismantled barriers protecting the outside of the Capitol building, and, at one point, Haffner allegedly used an aerosol spray against an officer with the U.S. Capitol Police guarding an outer door. Soon after, prosecutors say, Haffner, Loehrke and other rioters were able to breach the building through that door and can be seen in video footage taken inside the building. Haffner was arrested in Rapid City, S.D., on Dec. 1, 2021. (NPR)

Short narrative: Harlan Boen, faced arrest on January 5 2021, outside of the Wilson Building for allegedly carrying prohibited weapons, including a pistol without a license, and having unregistered ammunition. A police report said Boen had 14 cartridges of .40 caliber ammunition, a large capacity feeding device and a knife.
